item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Bertelsmann Foundation – Germany官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
NEW B |Brief - The Stakes of Stability: Electoral Reform in Italy

发布源: Bertelsmann Foundation – Germany | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Enter your email and customize your preferences.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s year did not go as expected.

In March, she championed a referendum that would havereformed the judicial system. Voters handilyrejected itfollowingcriticismthat it wouldconcentrate too much powerin the hands of the government. In July, Meloni suffered asurprise 188–187 defeaton an electoral reform package meant to take effect before next year’s parliamentary elections. The vote, cast via secret ballot, indicated that many within Meloni’s own coalition had defected on the measure.

Now, she may have finally notched a win. An amended,more expansive versionof the electoral reform that failed in July has passed in both theChamber of Deputiesand theSenate. As a result, Italy will shift to a fully proportional electoral system instead of the previous mixed system, under which one-third of deputies were still elected from first-past-the-post–based districts. Other new measures include a 3 percent threshold for single parties (10 percent for coalitions) to obtain seats and a requirement for parties or coalitions to name their candidate for prime minister prior to the election. The most impactful—and most controversial—reform in the package is the “majority prize.” Under the new rules, the first-place coalition will receive a bonus of 70 seats in the Chamber and 35 in the Senate if it reaches 42 percent of the vote in both houses, guaranteeing a majority.

Bertelsmann Stiftung

Enter your email and customize your preferences.

The Bertelsmann Stiftung was founded in 1977 by Reinhard Mohn as the result of social, corporate, and fiscal considerations. As the Bertelsmann Stiftung itself has put it, the foundation promotes “reform processes” and “the principles of entrepreneurial activity” to build a “future-oriented society.” Through its projects, studies and events, the Bertelsmann Stiftung stimulates debate and provides impetus for social change. Serving the public good and having a sustainable impact are the fundamental principles underlying its activities. The foundation’s initiatives not only generate solutions, they also provide empirically sound guidance for a broad public.

At present, the Bertelsmann Stiftung Executive Board consists of Dr. Ralph Heck (Chairman), Dr. Brigitte Mohn and Prof. Dr. Daniela Schwarzer.

item.content:encoded:
10 Nov 2026 / by David Bruce & Lizette LancasterCould a new agency stop crime syndicates infiltrating the police?Ahead of the Madlanga Commission’s recommendations, Parliament should carefully review South Africa’s capacity to investigate and prosecute serious crime.

发布源: 7. Institute for Security Studies – South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Published on 10 November 2026 inISS Today

ByDavid BruceIndependent Researcher and ISS ConsultantLizette LancasterHead, Justice and Violence Prevention, ISS Pretoria

For most of the post-apartheid period, there has been an ongoing debate in South Africa, sometimes extending to bitter political contestation, about how criminal justiceagenciescould better tackle serious crime. A key issue is how best to address state corruption, and whether to create a new body for the task.

Now, the Judicial Commission of Inquiry into Criminality, Political Interference, and Corruption in the Criminal Justice System (Madlanga Commission) has introduced new questions about organised crime and its role in police corruption. A notable concern, reflected in the commission’s terms ofreference, is the capture or infiltration of criminal justice agencies by crime syndicates.

In the debate about creating a new anti-corruption agency, a body established under Chapter 9 of the Constitution is widely seen in South Africa as the goldstandard. Chapter 9 organisations are accountable to Parliament rather than the Executive, and enjoy greater independence.

Existing Chapter 9 institutions are generally recognised as a mixed bag, with perhaps only the Auditor-General and Electoral Commission of South Africa seen as especially effective. That suggests Chapter 9 status alone does not guarantee success.

item.content:encoded:
Encuesta del IRI muestra un amplio respaldo de los…

发布源: International Republican Institute -- United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Caracas, Venezuela– Unaencuestanacional de opinión pública realizada por el Center for Insights in Survey Research del Instituto Republicano Internacional (IRI) revela que el 74 por ciento de los venezolanos considera que la democracia es la mejor forma de gobierno para su país, y el 62 por ciento desea un cambio importante en el sistema y el liderazgo político en los próximos 12 meses.

“Los venezolanos desean mayoritariamente un retorno a la democracia y un futuro mejor para su país”, afirmó Antonio Garrastazu, director sénior para América Latina y el Caribe del IRI. “Aunque existen distintas opiniones sobre cómo avanzar, hay una clara demanda de un cambio político significativo”.

Los encuestados estuvieron divididos sobre cuándo deberían celebrarse elecciones presidenciales. El 45 por ciento se mostró a favor de celebrar elecciones lo antes posible, mientras que el 52 por ciento señaló que deberían realizarse una vez que se cumplan ciertas condiciones, entre las cuales se mencionaron el vencimiento del período original en 2031 (24 por ciento), la liberación de todos los presos políticos (19 por ciento) y la recuperación económica (9 por ciento).

Al preguntarles cuáles son los desafíos más urgentes que enfrenta el país, el 40 por ciento de los encuestados señaló cuestiones económicas, entre ellas la situación económica general del país (22 por ciento), el costo de vida y los altos precios (14 por ciento), y el desempleo (4 por ciento).

item.content:encoded:
IRI Survey Shows Venezuelans Overwhelmingly Favor …

发布源: International Republican Institute -- United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Caracas, Venezuela– A nationwide public opinionsurveyconducted by the International Republican Institute’s (IRI) Center for Insights in Survey Research finds that 74 percent of Venezuelans view democracy as the best form of government for their country, and 62 percent want major changes to the political system and leadership in the next 12 months.

“Venezuelans overwhelmingly desire a return to democracy and a better future for their country,” said Antonio Garrastazu, Senior Director for Latin America and the Caribbean at IRI. “While views differ on the path forward, there is clear demand for meaningful political change.”

Respondents were divided on when elections should be held. Forty-five percent favored holding a vote as soon as possible, while 52 percent said elections should take place after certain conditions are met. These conditions included the expiration of the original term in 2031 (24 percent), the release of all political prisoners (19 percent), and economic recovery (9 percent).

When asked to identify the most pressing challenges facing the country, 40 percent of respondents cited economic issues, including the country’s general economic situation (22 percent), cost of living and high prices (14 percent), and unemployment (4 percent).

“Economic concerns remain front and center for many Venezuelans,” continued Garrastazu. “It is important that Venezuela’s economic recovery is prioritized alongside a return to democracy.”

More than 200 years of evidence show that free enterprise, free trade, property rights, and sound money can uplift people from every walk of life and every corner of the Earth.

Since 1990,over 1 billion people have been lifted out of extreme povertythanks to free trade.

On average,poverty rates are 3 timeslower in countries with sound money, compared to countries with chronic high inflation.

According to the Fraser Institute’s Economic Freedom of the World Annual Report,the average GDP per person in countries ranked in the top 25% for economic freedom was $52,877, while those in the bottom 25% averaged $6,968—a difference of 659%.

item.content:encoded:
COP31 and Climate Action’s New Centers of Gravity

发布源: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Council on Foreign Relations

Global Perspectives

COP31, the UN climate conference, begins in Turkey on November 9. Multilateral action on climate change is often at odds with the politics and policy agendas of individual states, even as the world is on track to surpass the 2°C (3.6°F) warming target laid out in the Paris Agreement.

Think tank experts from the Council of Councils provide insight into the status of global climate action and what we can expect from international cooperation.

Consensus-based climate negotiations are slow, especially as countries disagree over finance, responsibility, and the pace of change. Multilateralism—climate multilateralism, in particular—is in a tough spot.

The blame cannot all be laid at the door of the Trump administration. In Europe, political parties critical of development assistance and the impact of climate action on domestic competitiveness are becoming more prominent, while budgets are shifting toward defense spending. Energy security is the new watchword, both in the Global North and the Global South—a concept that can be used to justify switching away from fossil fuel imports, but equally to call for continued exploitation of domestic fossil fuel resources.

African-Born Lawmakers Had Breakout Success in the U.S. Midterms. Africa Is Watching.

发布源: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Council on Foreign Relations

Members of the Democratic Party are not the only ones celebrating the party’s stunning victory in last week’s midterm elections. Across Africa, where the exploits of African-born Americans are closely monitored, the outcome of the elections has generated considerable excitement. The reaction in Nigeria to the success offourteen Nigerian-Americansin various state-level elections—incidentally all on the platform of the Democratic Party—is typical. Nigerians in Diaspora Commission chairperson Abike Dabiri-Erewa went on social mediato congratulatethe victorious cohort, making sure to append a graphic vividly displaying their names, headshots, and respective constituencies.

In all, a recordtwenty-three African-born immigrantsfrom at least ten African countries spread across thirteen U.S. states won their respective races to become lawmakers in various American federal and state legislatures, extending a run that had seemed to reach a highwater mark back in January when Ugandan-born Zohran Mamdani became New York’s youngest mayor in over a century.

The feeling of pride among Africans is both justified and understandable. For many, the fact that African-born immigrants are finding their feet and flourishing across various walks of life is a welcome rebuke to racial bigots of all stripes who equate blackness with underachievement. item.content:encoded:
Global and Collective Health

发布源: BRICS Policy Center – Brazil | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The research program “Global and Collective Health” from BRICS Policy Center aims to foster critical and integrated studies on health issues, recognizing the structural inequalities that affect populations in BRICS countries. By connecting global health dynamics with local realities, we seek to qualitatively analyze the historical, socio-environmental, economic-commercial, cultural, and digital determinants that impact well-being and the promotion of health. Through an intersectional method and approach, the program seeks to understand how different categories – gender, race, class, territory, and religion – affect access and quality of healthcare across different national and local contexts. In this sense, the program constitutes a space for interdisciplinary, interregional, and inclusive dialogue, bringing together professionals, users, social movements, and governmental entities involved in the circulation of knowledge on global and collective health.

On an annual basis, the Reischauer Center hosts approximately 10-12 scholars, journalists, and policy practitioners from the major nations of Northeast Asia in Washington, DC. Visiting scholars spend several months to one year at the Reischauer Center conducting independent research, working with faculty members, and participating in ongoing events at Johns Hopkins SAIS. Scholars also occasionally present their research in the Visiting Scholar Brown-Bag Luncheons and make submissions to the Center’s various monograph series.

The Reischauer Center has recently welcomed visiting scholars from such organizations as: the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan (METI); the Ministry of Finance of Japan; the Ministry of Defense of Japan; Yomiuri Shimbun; Asahi Shimbun; Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO); the Mitsubishi Research Institute; and the Japan Institute of International Affairs.

item.content:encoded:
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

发布源: Brookings Institution | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Brookings Institution is committed to supporting inclusion and diversity across all aspects of our work. We recognize that to produce high-quality research that informs innovative, practical policy recommendations, we must strive for a workplace that represents diversity of experience, thought, and personal background. This means ensuring that everyone is heard and empowered to fully participate in Brookings’ mission to equip decisionmakers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

Since 2018, we have published annually our workplace and Board of Trustee demographics. We remain optimistic that through focus, transparency, and accountability, real progress on diversity and inclusion can be achieved over the long term. These annual reports represent one component of our work toward that end.

For the past seven years, Brookings employees have shared their experiences, skills, and connections through the Brookings Mentoring Program. The program is a nine-month experience where a mid- or late-career mentor is matched with one to three early or mid-career mentees. Every year, there is wide and varied participation; over 70 employees took part in 2025, which is more than 15% of Brookings’ total employee population. Mentor groups meet monthly to discuss topics like career development and feedback and enjoy all-group programming like networking events and expert panels. The REECA program will prepare you for a career that draws on broad area expertise, a high level of regional language proficiency, and superb research, writing, and communication skills. Our graduates go on to make meaningful contributions in their chosen field, whether in non-profits, academia, government, or the private sector.

Each REECA cohort includes eight to 10 students whose diverse academic, personal, and professional experiences inform their study of the region. While most REECA students major in international studies or a related field in college, some take a less traditional path to graduate school. They may have grown up and been educated in the region, spent a year or two working or volunteering there, or simply read every book they could find on a country of interest. Some REECA students serve in the U.S. Army and are training as foreign area officers. Whatever brought our students to us, they all share these qualities:

If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply to the program.

As a REECA student, you'll study the history, politics, society, and culture of the region, build a high level of proficiency in one or more relevant languages, and gain skills to help you succeed in your chosen career after graduation. Together with the director of graduate studies, you'll design an individual plan of study and revisit it before each new term to ensure that you make the most of your short time with us. item.title: [Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) -- Belgium] The Progressive Post
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) -- Belgium官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Progressive Post

发布源: Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) -- Belgium | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

In this nightmare vision of cats in revolt, fifteen-year-old Alex and his friends set out on a diabolical orgy of robbery, rape, torture and murder. Alex is jailed for his teenage delinquency and the State tries to reform him - but at what cost?

With regional powers like Israel, Turkey, the Gulf States and Egypt, becoming increasingly assertive in the Mediterranean, this issue'sSpecial CoverageThe crowded sea: fragmentation around the Mediterranean, focuses on the role the EU could and should play in this changing landscape.

No matter how fast we run, much like in Lewis Carroll'sThrough the Looking-Glass, we struggle to catch up with AI's innovations. In ourFocusThe red queen's race: running faster to match the pace of AI, we consider how to make AI socially, economically and democratically sustainable.

Our firstDossier,Beyond implementation day: the Pact on Migration and Asylumexamines the uncertainties surrounding the pact's execution  as well as the human rights concerns raised by the approval of the Return Regulation by the European Parliament. And the secondDossierThe EU's industrial paradigm shiftfocuses on the European Commission's newly proposed Industrial Accelerator Act. Even though a noticeably more interventionist industrial strategy is proposed, the exact nature of the industrial Europe that is being shaped remains questionable.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
A Conversation with Rep. Ami Bera:Sustaining U.S.–Japan–ROK Cooperation | READ MORE >

发布源: 7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

What does it take to maintain stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific over the next 75 years?

On November 20th, 2025, the Reischauer Center was honored to host Representative Ami Bera—Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific—for a conversation atJohns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS).

Representative Ami Bera stressed that, for the Indo-Pacific security in the 21st century, the US should deepen the cooperation with like-valued countries such as Japan and ROK. To strengthen U.S.–Japan–ROK trilateral ties with consistency, Representative Ami Bera believed this trilateral cooperation should be institutionalized through an ongoing legislative dialogue that can outlast political cycles.

Representative Ami Bera also explored supply-chain resilience, economic coercion, global health security, and the strategic implications of the Pacific Islands.

Grateful to Representative Bera, Dr. Calder, and to our engaged audience for this event!

On both sides of the Atlantic, partisan polarization increased, as populist and anti-immigrant issues and fallout of the Ukraine war dominated the 2024 campaigns. The speakers analyzed the commonalities and differences of the election results and in their wake, the likely course of policy and democracy.

Trackers and Indices

Our Millionaire Tracker monitors the outflow of millionaires from the UK. According to our analysis, the number of millionaires in the UK is at its lowest point since 2008.

Cost of Rent Day is the day when English renters stop paying rent and start putting their earnings into their own pocket.

Tax Freedom Day is the day when Britons stop paying tax and start putting their earnings into their own pocket.

Our State Reliance Index tracks the number of people who are reliant on the state for their livelihood. According to our latest analysis, 52.1% of British adults are reliant on the state for their livelihood.

Our State Pension Tracker forecasts when the National Insurance system will become unsustainable. Our estimate is that from 2036, NI obligations will exceed NI contributions.

Our Accountability Tracker monitors progress against the Government’s own stated goals, consolidating them into a single framework.

Our Electricity Tracker compares UK industrial electricity prices to those in France. It reveals that UK industrial electricity prices are 81% higher than in France.

The Global Energy Security Index 2026 ranks 187 countries on their ability to produce and procure reliable energy, assessing dispatchability, energy diversity, import security and ability to pay.

Compare estimated income tax and National Insurance with welfare spending across all 575 constituencies in England and Wales. Explore your area on our map.

Die Themenlinie befasst sich mit dem globalen Trend zur Autokratisierung und den Herausforderungen für die deutsche und europäische Politik.

Die Themenlinie widmet sich den umfassenden Veränderungen eines disruptiven wirtschaftlichen und technologischen Wandels, der für deutsche und europäische Politik Handlungszwänge und -möglichkeiten bedingt.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在IMANI Center for Policy and Education — Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Centre for Energy and Climate Policy

发布源: IMANI Center for Policy and Education — Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policyat IMANI is dedicated to finding lasting solutions to the persistent challenges in Ghana & Africa’s energy & climate sector. Despite numerous efforts to address the sector’s issues, progress has often fallen short due to a general lack of a comprehensive “follow through” approach. This underscores the need for remedial measures and their implementation to adopt a new direction and focus.

We believe that solving the energy & climate sector problems requires a multifaceted approach that includes thorough diagnosis of the sector’s issues, the development of innovative solutions, or the adoption of tried-and-tested remedial measures. Crucially, it also involves consistently tracking the implementation of these measures. This holistic approach informs our research and advocacy efforts at the Centre, ensuring that we contribute effectively to sustainable energy and climate policies in Ghana and across Africa.

Improving the Performance of State Actors in the Energy Sector-

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policy at IMANI Ghana assesses the performance of state actors in the energy sector. We evaluate public sector agencies responsible for energy based on key indicators such as transparency, efficiency, autonomy, and financial accountability. Through this comprehensive assessment, we aim to drive improvements and promote best practices within the sector, ensuring a sustainable and efficient energy landscape for Ghana and beyond.

Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning

发布源: Food, Agriculture and Natural Resources Policy Analysis Network (FANRPAN) – South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Strategic pillar 4

A system that tracks our results, holds us to account and helps us improve.

Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning, often shortened to MEAL, helps FANRPAN deliver on its mandate with transparency, efficiency and measurable results.

We are building one system for tracking progress, capturing lessons and improving every programme and thematic area. Data are collected in the same way across projects, countries learn from one another, and programmes change course when the evidence says they should.

This makes us more accountable to the governments, partners and communities we work with. It also makes our own decisions better informed.

From the Strategic Plan 2025 to 2035.

Define the indicators and measures that track performance and outcomes.

Use standard systems so that results are measured the same way in every project.

Support national data systems that serve the goals of agrifood systems transformation.

Use evaluation findings to refine strategies and make programmes work better.

The MEAL framework will not only enhance accountability but also strengthen evidence-informed decision-making.

FANRPAN Strategic Plan 2025 to 2035

From the results framework of the Strategic Plan.

A central MEAL system and framework in use across all projects

Data collection systems that track project performance and outcomes

Staff and partners with the skills to run MEAL processes

Monitoring results used for adaptive management and accountability

item.content:encoded:
Knowledge management and advocacy

发布源: Food, Agriculture and Natural Resources Policy Analysis Network (FANRPAN) – South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Strategic pillar 2

Better access to evidence that supports agrifood systems policy transformation.

Knowledge and advocacy

Policy has long been shaped mostly by the state, with little input from other actors.

FANRPAN works to give researchers, farmer organisations, agribusiness, parliamentarians and the media a stronger voice in agricultural and food policy debates. We turn complex evidence into products people can use, and bring stakeholders together in dialogue.

We also help countries and stakeholders understand continental frameworks, such as the African Continental Free Trade Area, the African Union climate change strategy and biodiversity frameworks.

From the Strategic Plan 2025 to 2035.

Keep up-to-date data systems on research outputs and the actors behind them.

Work with academic and research institutions to widen the reach of evidence.

Practical, context-relevant products that influence policy debate and decisions.

Bring stakeholders together to build shared understanding and coherent policy.

Dialogue is how FANRPAN turns evidence into shared positions.

From the results framework of the Strategic Plan.

Knowledge databases on policy research and stakeholders, kept up to date

Targeted advocacy and knowledge products for decision-makers

A digital platform for publishing and sharing agrifood policy research

Multi-stakeholder policy dialogues that build collaboration and shared understanding

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Food, Agriculture and Natural Resources Policy Analysis Network (FANRPAN) – South Africa官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Capacity strengthening

发布源: Food, Agriculture and Natural Resources Policy Analysis Network (FANRPAN) – South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Strategic pillar 3

Stronger institutions and people, able to engage with agrifood systems policy processes.

Capacity strengthening

FANRPAN strengthens the readiness of governments, civil society, research institutions and the private sector to help design, domesticate and implement major continental strategies.

Our focus is at country level. We work with state and non-state actors, including research institutions, farmers, agribusiness, civil society and the media, so that they can take part in policy with confidence.

We also strengthen our own network. National policy nodes and the Regional Secretariat need the skills and resources to convene and lead policy dialogue.

[Media Coverage] Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA)

发布源: Singapore Institute of International Affairs (SIIA) --Singapore | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Proposed changes to Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA) were discussed in Parliament on 4 November 2026, drawing wide local and international media coverage.

The amendments aim to strengthen Singapore’s ability to investigate and act against entities linked to transboundary haze, including through higher penalties and expanded enforcement measures.

Several leading outlets also quoted SIIA Chairman Simon Tay on the implications of the proposed changes and the continuing importance of regional cooperation.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centro de Implementacion de Politicas Publicas para la Equidad y el Crecimiento (CIPPEC) --Argentina官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Diálogos por la Docencia: continuamos la conversación con referentes legislativos

发布源: Centro de Implementacion de Politicas Publicas para la Equidad y el Crecimiento (CIPPEC) --Argentina | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

En el marco de la segunda etapa de Diálogos por la Docencia, CIPPEC reunió a 11 representantes del ámbito legislativo de diverso signo político. Diputados y senadores del Congreso Nacional, legisladores porteños y asesores compartieron sus ideas sobre cómo fortalecer la profesión docente. Esteban Torre, director del Programa de Educación, y Cecilia Veleda, investigadora principal del Programa, presentaron los acuerdos alcanzados en las mesas de trabajo desarrolladas entre marzo y julio de 2026.

Participaron del encuentro Mariela Coletta, Alicia Fregonese, Marina Salzmann, Nicolás Trotta, Maximiliano Ferraro, Blanca Osuna, Romina Del Plá, Maru Bielli, Sonia Rojas Decut, Mercedes Llano y Sabrina Ajmechet. Karina Banfi y Sergio Siciliano enviaron a sus asesores, que se sumaron al intercambio junto con los equipos de los legisladores presentes.

La primera etapa reunió a 50 referentes (docentes, exfuncionarios, especialistas e investigadores) y tuvo como resultado 25 acuerdos para fortalecer la profesión. Ahora, la iniciativa suma nuevas voces: autoridades nacionales y provinciales, sindicatos, redes docentes, universidades, familias y sociedad civil, y sector productivo.

El documento Diálogos por la Docencia, publicado en septiembre de 2026, fue elaborado por Esteban Torre, director del Programa de Educación; Cecilia Veleda, investigadora principal; Emmanuel Lista, investigador asociado; Carla Paparella, coordinadora, y Catalina Balbiani Pellegrini, analista. item.content:encoded:
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

发布源: Brookings Doha Center --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Brookings Institution is committed to supporting inclusion and diversity across all aspects of our work. We recognize that to produce high-quality research that informs innovative, practical policy recommendations, we must strive for a workplace that represents diversity of experience, thought, and personal background. This means ensuring that everyone is heard and empowered to fully participate in Brookings’ mission to equip decisionmakers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

Since 2018, we have published annually our workplace and Board of Trustee demographics. We remain optimistic that through focus, transparency, and accountability, real progress on diversity and inclusion can be achieved over the long term. These annual reports represent one component of our work toward that end.

For the past seven years, Brookings employees have shared their experiences, skills, and connections through the Brookings Mentoring Program. The program is a nine-month experience where a mid- or late-career mentor is matched with one to three early or mid-career mentees. Every year, there is wide and varied participation; over 70 employees took part in 2025, which is more than 15% of Brookings’ total employee population. Mentor groups meet monthly to discuss topics like career development and feedback and enjoy all-group programming like networking events and expert panels. Estudia y analiza la situación política, promueve la cultura democrática, una mayor participación de la sociedad civil en la toma de decisiones y el fortalecimiento de las instituciones democráticas.

Propicia la realización de conversatorios para acercar, informar y comprometer a los actores clave a implementar soluciones que fortalezcan al Estado y adecúen las instituciones a la realidad de una sociedad multicultural. Da seguimiento a los acontecimientos sociopolíticos en los ámbitos nacional y regional.

Publican, entre otros, la Monografía de Partidos Políticos, el Seminario Permanente sobre Estado y Sociedad en un Contexto Multicultural, la Monografía del Congreso de la República y analizan, cada cuatro años, el proceso electoral.

Se caracterizan por impulsar el análisis de coyuntura y la promoción del diálogo intersectorial.

Departamento de Análisis Jurídico (DAJ)

发布源: Asociación de Investigación y Estudios Sociales (ASIES) --Guatemala | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Promueve el fortalecimiento institucional del Estado democrático de Derecho en el marco de los principios y valores de la Constitución y los Acuerdos de Paz por medio del desarrollo de investigaciones, discusión y análisis de la realidad y los problemas nacionales.

Tiene a su cargo el desarrollo de actividades, proyectos y programas apoyan, de forma técnica, al Congreso.

Efectúa dictámenes, análisis, estudios y opiniones legislativas. Formula propuestas y da seguimiento a la agenda legislativa en materia de seguridad y justicia.

Para apoyar al proceso de fortalecimiento sistémico de la justicia realiza investigaciones, análisis y desarrollo de actividades, proyectos y programas de incidencia.

Da seguimiento periódico a sus avances y dificultades, con el fin de incidir en  políticas públicas y hacerlas cada vez más perfectibles para proteger derechos humanos de los habitantes del país.

Participa en las actividades y planes de trabajo de redes y consorcios como el Foro Guatemala, la Red Centroamericana de Centros de Pensamiento e Incidencia (LaRed), Convocatoria Ciudadana y Red Nacional de Formación e Investigación Ambiental (REDFIA).

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在United States Institute of Peace (USIP)官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Iran | United States

发布源: United States Institute of Peace (USIP) | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

On June 17, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Iran at the Palace of Versailles in France. The Memorandum declares an immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon. Both sides committed to refrain from initiating war or threatening force against one another and to respect each other’s sovereignty. The agreement opens a 60-day window, extendable by mutual consent, for negotiations toward a final deal.

Iran committed to arranging safe passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, at no charge, for 60 days. Simultaneously, the United States committed to begin removing its naval blockade immediately upon signing and to fully end it within 30 days. Iran reaffirmed that it will not procure or develop nuclear weapons

The White House stated that the agreement ensures Iran will never obtain a nuclear weapon and that any sanctions relief or economic benefits are strictly contingent on Iran’s continued compliance. The State Department has since identified the memorandum as a continuing regional priority alongside efforts to secure full and free transit through the Strait and support peace and stability in the region.

This page will be updated as negotiations progress.

“Most importantly, we have a deal that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” – President Donald J. Trump

“The President’s Peace Plan in Iran is Already Bearing Real Fruits For The American People.” – Vice President JD Vance

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Hudson Institute官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Is There an Effective “America First” Position on Israel?

发布源: Hudson Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Of course. Here it is.

Last Sunday, President Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection as prime minister of Israel, calling him a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” and an indispensable partner against Iran. “If Israel has the wrong Leader,” Trump warned, “America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so.” The following day, Vice President JD Vance pointedly declined to follow his lead. “I endorse American candidates,” Vance explained. This was an odd declaration from a vice president who traveled to Hungary earlier this year to campaign for Viktor Orbán. Apparently, endorsing foreign politicians is acceptable in Budapest but not in Jerusalem.

The disagreement raises a question that goes well beyond Netanyahu or Israeli electoral politics: What is the proper “America First” position on Israel? Trump has answered through his actions, taking American military cooperation with Israel to unprecedented heights and treating the Jewish state as a powerful partner against Iran. Vance’s position is more complicated. In a recent interview with Sean Spicer, he acknowledged having disagreed with Trump over the Iran war and expressed sympathy for Tucker Carlson’s anger about it. Carlson has depicted the war as a betrayal of American interests undertaken at Israel’s behest. The contrast between Trump and Vance therefore reaches beyond a disagreement over Netanyahu. Fewer than 40 percent of the venture capitalists who have made investments have ever funded a successful firm.

The researchers built a new dataset covering more than 100,000 professionals affiliated with US VC firms, including 37,000 investment professionals. They used large language models, supplemented with manual validation, to extract biographical details from archived VC firm websites over the period 1996 to 2025. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在National Bureau of Economic Research官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Bulletin on the Economics of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias

发布源: National Bureau of Economic Research | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Nearly one in ten older Americans lives with dementia, a condition that gradually erodes memory and the cognitive skills needed for complex decision-making. Even though Medicare coverage is nearly universal among this age group, traditional Medicare alone leaves significant gaps as it does not cover dental, vision, or hearing care, and it carries substantial cost-sharing. To fill these gaps, beneficiaries must actively choose among several insurance options—enrolling in Medicare Advantage, adding private supplemental insurance to traditional Medicare, or, for those with sufficiently low income and assets, applying for Medicaid. Beneficiaries may make changes during open enrollment each year and must re-enroll in private supplemental coverage or Medicare Advantage if their plan is no longer offered or they fail to pay premiums. Those who are eligible for Medicaid must recertify each year.

This annual decision-making process, which may involve interacting with multiple agencies, may be especially difficult for individuals whose cognitive abilities are declining. This may leave them with incomplete insurance protection at a time when they need it most. InSupplemental Medicare Insurance Coverage for Older Adults with Probable Dementia(NBER Working Paper 35606),Melissa McInerney,Lorena Moreno, andJennifer M. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在National Bureau of Economic Research官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Bulletin on Health

发布源: National Bureau of Economic Research | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Between 2010 and 2024, medical spending in the US grew from 17.2 percent of GDP to 18.0 percent. This growth was substantially below both historical precedent and actuarial projections by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). By 2024, annual healthcare expenditures were nearly $1 trillion (15 percent) below the 2010 projections.

InHas the United States Bent the Health Care Cost Curve?(NBER Working Paper 35231),David M. CutlerandLev R. Klarnetexamine potential explanations for this sustained period of slower growth. They compare actual expenditures to the 2010 CMS actuarial forecast, adjusting for differences between anticipated and realized inflation. Because the slowdown was evident across all payers, the researchers focus their analysis on the total market for medical care goods and services. They decompose the overall slowdown into differences that are attributable to utilization, prices, long-run supply, and technological change.

Cost-saving technology and changes in insurance design that affect utilization have reduced expenditures relative to projections 15 years ago.

Slower growth in the quantity of care is the most important contributor to the overall slowdown. Utilization changes account for at least 28 percent of the overall slowdown and explain at least $272 billion of the difference between actual spending in 2024 and the 2010 forecast. PHOENIX, Ariz.(August 24, 2026) – Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs has proclaimed August 24–30, 2026, as the third annual John McCain Democracy Week, honoring Senator John McCain’s legacy of service and his lifelong commitment to freedom, democracy, and human rights.

The week coincides with what would have been Senator McCain’s 90th birthday on August 29. It also comes as the United States celebrates its 250thanniversary, providing an opportunity to reflect on the ideals that shaped the nation, guided Senator McCain throughout his life, and continue to call each generation to defend them.

“Senator John McCain embodied the very best of Arizona—a fierce independence, an unwavering devotion to country over party, and a strong commitment to protecting our democratic institutions. I’m proud to proclaim this week John McCain Democracy Week as a reminder that our democracy requires courage, civility, and a shared willingness to serve a cause greater than ourselves,”said Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs.

Marking eight years since his passing, the proclamation recognizes Senator McCain’s belief that America is a nation defined by its commitment to democratic ideals, freedom, and the rights of individuals to determine their own futures. He often reminded Americans that our shared values and democratic principles are greater than our differences.

item.title: [Lugar Center] EU Report: Still no problems with Cardin-Lugar
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Lugar Center官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
EU Report: Still no problems with Cardin-Lugar

发布源: Lugar Center | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The European Union recently released its latest review of the EU version of the Cardin-Lugar legislation that requires oil, gas and mining companies to report their payments to governments. The bottom line: the reporting requirements, which have been in place now for five years, have imposed no competitive harm on the companies and pose no threat to European energy security.

The big news here: this is no news to most people who have been following implementation of Cardin-Lugar type laws around the world. Earlier reviews by Canada, Britain and the EU—all of which, along with Switzerland and Norway, passed anti-corruption reporting requirements modeled on the 2010 Cardin-Lugar legislation, Sec. 1504 of the Dodd-Frank financial reform bill—had found the same thing. Many major international oil companies have publicly come to the identical conclusion, and have said the compliance costs are minimal.

However, there are some people for whom this is apparently novel information: namely the two Republican commissioners of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Hester Peirce and Elad Roisman. They voted (along with then-Chair Jay Clayton, a Trump appointee) late last year to approve a watered down version of the regulation implementing Cardin-Lugar, badly out of step with the EU.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Lugar Center官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Self-Preservation, Not Evaluation Drives Supreme Court Confirmation Vote

发布源: Lugar Center | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Senate will soon have a chance to vote on the nomination of Ketanji Brown Jackson to be a Supreme Court justice.  There will be much debate about the nominee’s credentials and judicial philosophy.  Senators will muse about whether she is sufficiently faithful to the Constitution and whether she will be overly activist.  They will probe her past decisions and her judicial temperament.  But the process is for show.  Almost all Republicans knew how they would vote on Biden’s nominee, even before he announced it would be Jackson.  The aim of Republican research will be constructing plausible justifications for opposing her, rather than seriously considering her merits.

Senators of both parties grasp the unfortunate reality that no vote is more likely to crash their reputation with their base voters than supporting a Supreme Court nominee of the other party.  SCOTUS nominations have become proxies for the entire range of hot-button issues that animate American partisanship, from abortion and guns to immigration and voting rights.

This phenomenon has accompanied the plunge in bipartisanship during the internet age.  Through the end of the 20th century, Senators voted according to a presumption that Supreme Court nominees deserved confirmation unless they were unqualified or afflicted with a scandal, a conflict of interest, or a deep character flaw.  Some historians point to the 1987 nomination of Robert Bork as the pivotal event in the politicization of Supreme Court confirmati

ByAnnMarie Pariseau

MIDLAND, Mich. — The Mackinac Center for Public Policy’s board of directors unanimously selected Michael J. Reitz, the organization’s executive vice president, to become its next president on Jan. 1, 2027. Reitz will succeed Joseph G. Lehman, who has led the Center for 18 years and will become president emeritus.

Lehman will continue working full-time for the Center in his new role. He will stay closely engaged with Mackinac Center supporters, deliver speeches and continue writing. He will also remain on the board of directors.

“On behalf of the board, I thank Joe Lehman for his friendship, character and strategic leadership in bringing the Mackinac Center to where it is today,” said Board Chairman Rodney Lockwood. “Joe built a strong organization with a deep bench of talent, and Mike Reitz is the board’s enthusiastic and unanimous choice to lead the organization as we celebrate our 40th anniversary.”

Lehman joined the Mackinac Center in 1995, serving as president since 2008. Under his leadership, and with the support of its many friends, the organization won major policy victories across four governors’ administrations through legislation, court decisions and shifts in public opinion. item.content:encoded:
Some ways new Michigan leadership can encourage more housing

发布源: Mackinac Center | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

ByJarrett Skorup

Demand for housing in Michigan has outstripped supply and led to higher prices. The solution to this is simple: Build more. But it is difficult because of government and market obstacles.

And despite massive government subsidies for more apartments, housing construction has barely budged for years. And we don’t build nearly as much as we did even in the 1990s.

The government isn’t particularly good at knowing how much or what types of housing needs to be built. But the market is good at it. It is unfortunate that so many rules and regulations have arisen that make iteffectively illegaleven to build much of the housing people in Michigan are currently living in.

Here are some ways to change that.

The Mercatus Center has released amenuof proven policy options state lawmakers can use to lower the cost of housing. This includes eliminating parking mandates, making it easier to build starter homes and accessory dwelling units, putting in place better guidelines for zoning, and updating construction standards and building codes.

The American Enterprise Institute also recently released a dashboard with a section on “The Case for Ending the Ban on Starter Homes.” The report estimates that zoning regulations prevented 3.4 million starter homes from being built over the past decade. Many local governments put in place minimum home and minimum lot size regulations that make it difficult or impossible to build smaller, less expensive homes.

The Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies (FSI) is pleased to announce that James Fearon will serve as the next co-director of the institute’s Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC), effective September 16, 2026.

Fearonis currently the Theodore and Frances Geballe Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences, a professor of political science, and a senior fellow at FSI, where he is affiliated with both CISAC and the Center on Democracy, Development and the Rule of Law. In 2021 and 2022, he served as a senior advisor in the U.S. Department of Defense, working primarily on the 2022 National Defense Strategy and its implementation within the Department.

He is the author of several highly influential studies of the causes of interstate and civil war, signaling and bargaining in interstate disputes, and deterrence theory. Earlier this year he published the bookWorse than War: The Global Costs of Violence(Princeton University Press), co-authored with Anke Hoeffler, that estimates and compares the prevalence and costs of war with the prevalence and costs of interpersonal violence. His current work includes research on how U.S. and Chinese defense postures affect risks of escalation in the western Pacific; AI and the stability of nuclear deterrence; and the organizational design of defense bureaucracies. Across Africa, law enforcement officers have detected, intercepted and dismantled numerous drug laboratories, many of which were used for the mass production of methamphetamine drugs also known as meth, or crystal meth. item.content:encoded:
The History of Pacific Forum

发布源: Pacific Forum | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Pacific Forum is one of the world’s leading Asia-Pacific policy research institutes and was one of the first organizations in the United States to focus exclusively on this region. The inspiration for the organization first came in November 1943, when then-Lieutenant Lloyd R. “Joe” Vasey was aboard the submarine USSGunnel. In Vasey’s own words:

After successfully attacking a convoy of enemy ships in the Yellow Sea between Korea and Japan, the American submarine USS Gunnel was worked over by Japanese anti-submarine warships during a 36-hour ordeal, with explosions from depth bombs periodically jolting the submarine severely.

“After surfacing at midpoint during darkness to replenish the foul air, Gunnel was sighted and attacked by gunfire from the three warships. While submerging again, Gunnel torpedoed one of the three warships, which was rapidly closing at close range. Several hours later, with depleted air and battery power and no other option but to surface, the Commanding Officer, Lieut. Commander John S. McCain Jr., USN, called his officers together, and all agreed to fight it out in a surface gun battle with the enemy warships rather than surrender.“While climbing the 22-foot vertical ladder to the bridge hatch while surfacing, the submarine’s Torpedo Officer, Lt. Lloyd “Joe” Vasey, thought to himself, “there have to be better ways to resolve international disputes” and vowed that if he survived, he would one day strive to do something about it.

November 05, 2026Supreme Court Asked to Allow Removal of Dangerous Alien Criminals

发布源: Federation for American Immigration Reform | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

WASHINGTON— The Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) has filed abriefin the U.S. Supreme Court urging it to overturn a lower-court injunction stopping the ongoing removal of a class of dangerous alien criminals to nations other than their home countries.

The aliens—who have been convicted of such crimes as child sexual assault, sexual abuse of the mentally disabled, and murder—claimed that if they were removed to their home countries, they would face torture. But when federal officials asked them if they would consent to being removed to nations such as South Sudan—countries that have agreed to take them—instead, they said yes. Nevertheless, the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts enjoined their removal as inconsistent with this country’s treaty obligations under the Convention Against Torture (CAT), and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit affirmed.

As FAIR shows in its brief, however, the appellate court failed to show how the removals were inconsistent with CAT. Instead, it rewrote and added to the regulations under which such removals are carried out—which implement CAT as directed by Congress and therefore have the force of law—by claiming that the regulations require individualized diplomatic assurances that a given alien will not be tortured. After months of unexplained delays, the DMV invoiced FAIR more than $2,000 to process four of the five items, accepted payment, and then reversed course. LOS ANGELES, Oct. 20, 2026 – Futurology, the Berggruen Institute’s podcast about the forces reshaping how we live, think and govern ourselves, has won Gold in the Conversation Starter category of the 5th Annual Signal Awards, announced today.

Each week, Futurology hosts conversations that illuminate how the concepts changing our world every day have outrun the words we have to describe them.

Those conversations span science, philosophy, technology, politics, and culture. Episodes have taken up the fate of the liberal world order, the search for life beyond Earth, the ethics of rewriting the human genome, the economics of attention, the nature of consciousness, and what organized religion makes of artificial minds.

In its first year, Futurology has put more than 50 thinkers on the record in front of millions of viewers and listeners. Guests have included political scientist Francis Fukuyama, Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna, mathematician Terence Tao, novelist Elif Shafak, philosopher Michael Sandel, and AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li.

“At the Berggruen Institute we have always believed that the paradigms of our new world will come from the world of ideas. This recognition by the Signal Awards tells us that we are not alone in that thinking, that audiences are hungry for something deeper and longer-term than the news cycle. This is meaningful. item.content:encoded:
Working PaperNo. No. 1133October 19, 2026Finance, Capitalist Evolution, and Structural Reform: A Backwards Perspective on Hyman P. MinskyRiccardo Bellofiore

发布源: Levy Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Thirty years after Hyman Minsky’s death, his name is more familiar than his economics. The notion of a “Minsky moment” has helped restore financial instability to macroeconomics, but it has also encouraged a narrowing of Minsky to the proposition that prolonged stability generates leverage, speculation and eventually crisis. This essay adopts a backwards perspective on Minsky. It starts from the later work on money manager capitalism, the New Deal, structural reform, the employer of last resort and the socialization of investment and returns from there to the Wall Street paradigm and the Financial Instability Hypothesis. Seen from this perspective, financial instability appears as one element of a broader theory of capitalist evolution in which financial structures, institutions, policy interventions and the organization of production change together.

I distinguish here between reading, interpretation and reconstruction. A reading stays close to Minsky’s texts and does not remove their tensions, shifts and occasional ambiguities in order to produce a retrospective consistency. An interpretation goes further: it tries to recover the internal logic connecting apparently separate parts of his work. On this level, the financial theory of investment, the Financial Instability Hypothesis, endogenous money, the stage view of capitalism, Big Government and Big Bank, and the later program of structural reform belong to the same evolving project. 发布源: Levy Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The monetary policy tightening cycle is underway: the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) unanimously decided to raise rates at its September meeting and is on track to raise them again, at least once more in 2026. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh had already indicated a more hawkish stance during his Jackson Holespeech, arguing that “[p]rice stability is not self-executing, nor is inflation necessarily mean-reverting.” He further reiterated that “[i]t is the Fed’s job to deliver stable prices,” and reinforced the Fed’s commitment to the 2 percent inflation target as a “firm, fixed target.” Even voices typically dovish on monetary policy were calling for a small rate hike before the Fed meeting.

Those in favor of a hike believe that rising inflation in recent months points to a widespread problem that is becoming hard to uproot. While it’s almost never clearly explained how hiking rates by 25 or even 75 basis points will move us toward the inflation target, hike the Fed must, lest it put its credibility at stake. Yet Warsh didn’t seem to believe that questions abouthowmonetary policy was going to tackle inflation merited an answer during his post-FOMC Q&A with reporters.

In March of 2022we arguedthat raising rates was the wrong medicine for the pandemic’s inflation. We warned that high rates would do nothing to solve the supply-side problems the economy was facing. item.content:encoded:
Global Thinkers Series: Ethical Intelligence

发布源: Berggruen Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Capacities and activities once considered exclusively human—such as solving complex mathematical problems, translating between languages, and even identifying emotional patterns in complex datasets—are now being performed by AI systems that increasingly outperform humans in these domains.

AI is currently undergoing a fundamental transformation, moving beyond the paradigm of automation historically associated with Alan Turing toward anemotional turnin the wake of the large language model (LLM) revolution.This shift opens up a new perspective on AI ethics.

The concept ofEthical Intelligenceenvisions AI systems that can identify and interpret patterns of ethical values emerging from human interactions and social practices. Such systems could create a new interface between AI and society, helping us develop our capacities for ethical reflection, judgment, and action.

What setsEthical Intelligenceapart from earlier approaches to AI ethics? What would it take to turn this vision into practice? How might AI transform not only what we do, but how we think and act? And how could it help us become more thoughtful, responsible human beings?

Chair in Epistemology, Modern and Contemporary Philosophy and Director of the International Center for Philosophy, the University of Bonn

Policy NoteNo. 2026/9October 14, 2026Smoothing the Stress Test: Averaging Reduces Capital Requirement Volatility, Not FragilityJuan Matias De Lucchi

发布源: Levy Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

On September 30, 2026, the Fed decided that, starting with the 2028 cycle, each large bank’s stress capital buffer will be set on the basis of the average of its two most recent supervisory stress tests rather than on the latest one alone. The stated goal is to reduce year-to-year volatility in capital requirements.

Averaging does reduce the volatility of capital requirements, but not necessarily financial fragility. This note argues that the main weakness lies in the stress test itself. First, it registers the flow of income that high interest rates bring to banks, but not the valuation losses they cause on the stock of assets. Second, its scenario rules out a recession in which rates stay high, because it implicitly treats inflation as demand-driven. Since projected capital declines have become shallower in recent tests, averaging would be slightly more demanding today—but only because the test itself understates the risks of high rates. Once those risks show up in the test, averaging will slow the system’s response: capital requirements will rise more slowly than the risk they are meant to cover.

Bank capital requirements are expressed as a ratio. The numerator is common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital—essentially shareholders’ equity. The denominator is risk-weighted assets (RWA), in which each asset counts according to its regulatory riskiness: 0 percent for Treasury securities, 50 percent for most mortgages, 100 percent for most corporate loans. item.content:encoded:
UCLA x Berggruen Institute2026 Berggruen Governance IndexLearn more

发布源: Berggruen Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Berggruen Governance Index (BGI) analyzes the relationship between democratic accountability, state capacity, and the provision of public goods. It builds upon prior work that examined the impact of governance and democracy on the quality of life. It is a collaborative project between the UCLA Luskin School of Public Affairs, the Hertie School, and the Berggruen Institute.

The Berggruen Governance Index (BGI) measures the quality of democracy, government, and life across 145 countries, drawing on data covering democratic accountability, state capacity, and public goods delivery. The 2026 BGI finds that while the world has not become more democratic since 2000 and the quality of government has shown no consistent improvement, the quality of life has generally risen. The unbalanced nature of these gains raises questions about their sustainability. The BGI analysis reveals that the 145 countries fall into one of four “governance worlds.” We call these the Consolidated Democratic States, Capacity-Constrained States, Authoritarian and Hybrid States, and Low-Capacity Developing States. Countries rarely cross between worlds, but substantial movement occurs within them. item.content:encoded:
November 05, 2026FAIR Urges Supreme Court to Unblock Wall

发布源: Federation for American Immigration Reform | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

WASHINGTON—The Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) has filed abriefin the U.S. Supreme Court urging it to suspend an injunction by the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas. The injunction blocks the federal government from waiving environmental and other requirements that would otherwise stand in the way of border wall construction in the Big Bend sector of the U.S.-Mexico border.

As FAIR shows in its brief, the courts lack jurisdiction to review such waivers and thereby block wall construction, unless there has been a violation of the Constitution. Here, the district court purported to base its injunction on a violation of the major questions doctrine, which it claimed is a constitutional doctrine.

As FAIR explains, however, the major questions doctrine is a Supreme Court-made rule against complicated statutory interpretations giving agencies vast new powers that were likely not foreseen or intended by Congress. It is not a constitutional doctrine. Even if it were, it does not even apply to this case, where the only statutory issue is the simple one of whether the illegal entries through the Big Bend sector have been, as the waiver provision requires, “high.”

发布源: J Street | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

From electing pro-peace candidates to building grassroots power in key states, J Street's political programs work together to advance our vision for a safer, more democratic future.

Want to get in contact with J Street's Political Team? Please email PAC@jstreet.org.

The J Street Action Fund, our independent expenditure arm, reached more than 1,000,000 voters in two of the country’s most competitive Congressional districts in 2024.

JStreetPAC advances our work in Congress by supporting pro-Israel, pro-peace, and pro-democracy candidates. In the 2024 cycle, JStreetPAC distributed nearly $15 million to its endorsed candidates, our highest ever disbursement in an election cycle. In the 2024 cycle, JStreetPAC endorsed a majority of Democratic incumbents in both the House and Senate, demonstrating that we are the mainstream of the Democratic Party.

Long-term grassroots organizing is key to building political power and ensuring our democracy reflects the voices of all Americans. As such, we’re proud to announce that J Street members can now directly support organizing efforts in Pennsylvania, Georgia, North Carolina, and New Mexico through our grassroots partners for the 2026 cycle. To maximize our impact, we’re partnering with both statewide organizing hubs and select local organizations doing strategic civic engagement work.

item.content:encoded:
Transparencia y rendición de cuentas

发布源: Instituto de Estudios Peruanos --Peru | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

En el Instituto de Estudios Peruanos, la transparencia es un pilar fundamental de nuestra gestión institucional. A través de esta sección, ponemos a disposición del público información clara y accesible sobre nuestras auditorias, declaraciones, financiamiento y políticas internas, reafirmando nuestro compromiso con la integridad y la rendición de cuentas.

Los estudios y las actividades que desarrolla el IEP se realizan gracias al apoyo de diversas fuentes de financiamiento, entre las que se encuentran fundaciones privadas dedicadas a la investigación y el desarrollo, embajadas y organismos de cooperación internacional, así como instituciones peruanas públicas y privadas. Además, las diversas consultorías que realizan nuestros miembros asociados con organismos e instituciones de diversas partes del mundo, le proporcionan al Instituto fondos adicionales que le permiten avanzar hacia sus objetivos. De otro lado, la intensa labor editorial del IEP también brinda recursos que posibilitan la realización de las actividades de su Fondo Editorial.

发布源: Dejusticia --Colombia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Su creación significó la apertura de un nuevo campo de investigación en el área dejudicial politics, es decir, estudios multidisciplinarios basados en información y procesamientos novedosos sobre asuntos clave de la administración de justicia.

Es una plataforma pionera en el país, basada en un proceso de investigación participativa y aplicada, que garantiza su relevancia y la utilidad de sus hallazgos para la toma de decisiones del conglomerado judicial.Se inauguró en 2011 con la firma del “Convenio Marco entre el Poder Judicial y el Consejo Nacional de Rectores-Programa Estado de la Nación”.A la fecha se han publicado dos informes.

Ha realizado investigaciones en temas políticos, tanto a nivel nacional como regional. Actualmente es la Coordinadora de Investigación del Informe Estado de la Justicia. Analizamos y evaluamosel impacto de las políticas gubernamentalesy de los proyectos legislativos en la libertad económica y en el funcionamiento  de la economía, en cuanto a consumo, ahorro, producción e inversión.Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar publicaciones académicas que permitanincidir en la  formulación de políticas e iniciativas legislativasque promuevan la libertad económica y garanticen la democracia liberal.

Elaboramos documentos de análisis desde una perspectiva de libre mercado, evaluando elcomportamiento de la economía a partir de indicadores y el impacto de políticas económicas.

Participamos en la consolidación deíndices internacionalesque miden el desempeño del país en temas económicos y sociales de interés global.

Organizamos espacios de conversación como mesas redondas, foros y webinars para analizar asuntos de impacto económico. Contamos con la participación de expertos e invitados nacionales e internacionales de diferentes sectores.

Visualizamos nuestros hallazgos mediante boletines económicos, documentos de análisis de coyuntura, artículos de investigación, comunicados de prensa, videos y entrevistas.

item.title: [Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia] Índice de Competitividad Fiscal 2026: Colombia sigue entre los últimos de la OCDE por cómo grava el capital
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Índice de Competitividad Fiscal 2026: Colombia sigue entre los últimos de la OCDE por cómo grava el capital

发布源: Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

|22 de octubrede 2026

Lectura del Instituto de Ciencia Política Hernán Echavarría Olózaga sobre losresultados del Índice de Competitividad Fiscal 2026 publicados por Tax Foundation

El Instituto de Ciencia Política Hernán Echavarría Olózaga (ICP) analiza las debilidades del sistema tributario colombiano a partir de los resultados delÍndice de Competitividad Fiscal 2026. El documento advierte que las cargas sobre el capital y las dificultades para deducir los costos de inversión encarecen la actividad empresarial, afectan especialmente a las empresas nuevas y pequeñas y limitan la productividad y la generación de empleo.

El análisis señala que este deterioro se ha acumulado durante varios gobiernos, en medio de sucesivas reformas tributarias y un creciente gasto público. Frente a este panorama, el ICP propone simplificar el sistema tributario, ampliar las bases gravables, garantizar estabilidad normativa y revisar el gasto público para favorecer la inversión y el crecimiento económico.

The newspaper The Economist published a full page report on the project "Do-gooders and Do-besters"

No nation can tackle all problems at once. Resources are limited, including money, time, manpower and attention. Hence, it might make sense to first focus where the used resources can achieve the highest impacts on welfare.

This work has been produced as a part of the project Prioritizing best buys for development across the African continent by theCopenhagen Consensus.This reportgives African nations a first glimpse of where extra money can be best spent first. It is a fast-track analysis of some of the best policies across the continent, analyzed in time for the Grand Challenges Summit in Addis Ababa 27-30 October.

This publication aims to identify some of the best policies for Africa. Some of these policies can readily be implemented or scaled up with existing technology. These policies are outlined in this section of the report.

Other policies are good candidates for investment in R&D to develop new technologies that can make deployment much more feasible. These policies are described in thesecond sectionof this report.

For both sets of policies, this report uses social cost-benefit analysis to find the best policies. For any policy, we estimate the total costs.

A Scorecard For Humanity

发布源: Copenhagen Consensus Center --Denmark | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Bjørn Lomborg presented the Scorecard for Humanity  at TED headquarters in New York in October 2013

This unique research project has estimated the global costs of major problems from 1900 to 2050.

A Scorecard for Humanity fits into the ongoing conversation between optimists and pessimists for the last half century. The central question has been: what is the state of the world? The worries of overpopulation, starvation, pollution and running-out-of-everything staked out the pessimist case. The happy-go-lucky attitude gloating in the infallibleness of the market economy stood for the optimists. The results of our study have been published by Cambridge University Press under the book titleHow Much Have Global Problems Cost the World? A Scorecard from 1900 to 2050

"This book is a bracing tonic. An excellent survey for students, teachers, and the general public with a wealth of thought-provoking material. If you want to know how the world is doing, and get hard, comparable numbers to back it up, this is where to go."

-Alix Peterson Zwane, Executive Director, Evidence Action and the Deworm the World Initiative; Former Senior Program Officer on the Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene team, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation

BSEC Family of Institutions

发布源: International Centre for Black Sea Studies --Greece | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC)is a full-fledged intergovernmental, regional economic organization, established in 1992, with the aim to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Black Sea region. It consists of 13 Members States (Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Greece, Republic of Moldova, Republic of North Macedonia, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine). BSEC has more than 25 areas of cooperation, among them agriculture and agro-industry, banking and finance, combating organized crime, culture, education, emergency assistance, energy, environmental protection, healthcare and pharmaceutics, ICT, institutional renewal and good governance, science and technology, SMEs, tourism, trade and transport. The BSEC Permanent International Secretariat (PERMIS) is located in Istanbul, Turkey.

Parliamentary Assembly of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (PABSEC)is composed of 77 parliamentarians representing the 12 BSEC Member States. Established in 1993 as an inter-parliamentary consultative body, the Assembly has united the efforts of the national parliaments to ensure cooperation and partnership in the region, by providing legislative support for the implementation of the decisions taken by the Heads of State or Government or by the Ministers of Foreign Affairs. The PABSEC International Secretariat is seated in Istanbul, Turkey.

item.content:encoded:
Historia, Misión y Visión

发布源: Fundación Jaime Guzmán --Chile | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Fundación Jaime Guzmán

Desde 1991, trabajamos para que el ideario de Jaime Guzmán siga formando e inspirando a las futuras generaciones de servidores públicos en Chile.

Nuestra historia

La Fundación se creó en 1991, tras el asesinato de Jaime Guzmán, con el objetivo de que el ideario del senador formara e inspirara a las futuras generaciones.

La primera etapa de trabajo consistió en recopilar y organizar la biblioteca y el archivo personal de Jaime, material que ha sido la base del trabajo de difusión de su obra. Fieles a la preocupación que Jaime Guzmán siempre tuvo por los jóvenes —y movidos por la certeza de que el país necesita gente preparada para influir en los destinos de la Patria— la Fundación inició diversos programas con el propósito de capacitar y formar a quienes se sintieran atraídos por la idea de servir a Chile.

Así se creó elBachillerato en Servicio Públicoy se comenzaron a realizar seminarios y cursos formativos a lo largo de todo el país. A medida que la Fundación fue creciendo, se vio la oportunidad de promover nuestros ideales, especialmente en aquellos lugares donde por falta de recursos no podían contratar profesionales de excelencia. Fue así como un pequeño grupo de profesionales jóvenes, comprometido con derrotar la pobreza y convencido de que podían aportar a la prosperidad de Chile a través de sus talentos, decidió irse a trabajar a comunas apartadas y de escasos recursos.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PublicationFirst Independent Monitoring Report on the Implementation of the Reform AgendaRead more

发布源: 9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

This report presents the findings of the first independent monitoring efforts carried out by the NCEU Intersectoral Working Group (IWG) on the implementation of the Reform Agenda of the Republic of Serbia under the Reform and Growth Facility (RGF). The report covers thirty-seven reform steps due by 31 December 2025, across four out of the five policy areas of the Reform Agenda: Business Environment and Development of the Private Sector (7 steps), Green Transition – Energy (8 steps), Digital Transition (8 steps), and Fundamentals (14 steps). The Human Capital policy area does not include any reform steps with deadlines falling within this monitoring cycle. Three of the thirty-seven steps were approved by the European Commission in its first payment assessment in January 2026; this report reviews them from the perspective of the sustainability of reform results. For the remaining thirty-four steps, the IWG provides a detailed implementation assessment. The assessment draws on thirty-seven step-level monitoring reports prepared by the IWG’s six subgroup coordinators, as well as on official sources, independent monitoring outputs, and the coordinators’ direct involvement in the reform processes under review.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PublicationShadow Report on the Kosovo-Serbia Normalisation ProcessClick Here

发布源: 9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

This Shadow Report is the first independent, jointly produced assessment of the Agreement on the Path to Normalisation implementation, written simultaneously from Belgrade and Pristina. Its central contribution is theNormalisation Index– an original, replicable twin-component tool measuring (1) implementation of each Agreement and Annex commitment by Serbia, Kosovo*, and the EU, and (2) the engagement of the EU and the United States across four phases between 2023 and 2026. The Report combines the Index with structured fieldwork, focus groups, and desk research to identify six structural challenges behind the implementation gap, and translates them into five sets of actor-specific recommendations for the EU, the US, Serbia, Kosovo, and civil society.

Its overarching finding is stark: three years after Ohrid, overall Agreement implementation stands at just 21.1%, driven far more by external EU facilitation than by genuine political will on either side. The normalisation process has stalled not because political will is temporarily absent, but because the architecture of the process: unsigned commitments, ambiguous language, weak conditionality, and asymmetric incentives: has made non-implementation rational for both governments and unenforceable for the facilitator.

*This designation is without prejudice to positions on status and is in line with UNSCR 1244 and the ICJ opinion on Kosovo Declaration of Independence”

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在45. Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF) --Kosovo官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Prezantohet Fondi për Përkrahje Emergjente, në diskutimin mbi hapësirën qytetare nën presion

发布源: 45. Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF) --Kosovo | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Trina Binaku, koordinatore e granteve në KCSF, mori pjesë në sesionin interaktiv online“Hapësira qytetare nën presion: Nga rreziku te mbrojtja”, organizuar nga SCiDEV, i cili trajtoi sfidat dhe rreziqet me të cilat përballen aktivistët, gazetarët dhe organizatat e shoqërisë civile në ushtrimin e angazhimit të tyre qytetar, me fokus të veçantë në kontekstin e Shqipërisë.

Takimi ofroi një hapësirë praktike diskutimi mbi sigurinë fizike dhe digjitale, duke trajtuar çështje si sulmet online, cenimi i llogarive digjitale dhe frikësimi gjatë aktiviteteve publike. Gjithashtu, u diskutua për mënyrat e mbrojtjes nga këto rreziqe dhe mundësitë për të kërkuar mbështetje në situata emergjente.

Gjatë sesionit, Trina prezantoiFondin për Përkrahje Emergjente të Shoqërisë Civile (Civic Emergency Fund), një mekanizëm i reagimit të shpejtë që ofron mbështetje fleksibile për organizatat e shoqërisë civile, aktivistët, mediat e pavarura dhe nismat jo – formale që përballen me kërcënime për shkak të punës së tyre.

Fondi, i zbatuar nga KCSF dhe Trag Foundation në shtatë vende të Ballkanit Perëndimor, synon t’u mundësojë shoqërisë civile të përballojnë situatat emergjente dhe të vazhdojnë angazhimin e tyre në mënyrë të sigurt edhe në kohë krize.

Për më shumë mbi fondin, vizitoniwww.civicemergencyfund.com.
