item.title: [45. Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF) --Kosovo] Puka: Pjesëmarrja e shoqërisë civile duhet të ndikojë realisht në procesin e zgjerimit të BE-së
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在45. Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF) --Kosovo官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Puka: Pjesëmarrja e shoqërisë civile duhet të ndikojë realisht në procesin e zgjerimit të BE-së

发布源: 45. Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF) --Kosovo | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Dren Puka ngaKCSFpo merr pjesë në Civil Society & Think Tank Forum (CSF) 2026 që po mbahet në Prishtinë.

Në kuadër të forumit, ai ishte pjesë e panelit “Mbrojtja e hapësirës qytetare dhe demokracisë: nga zotimet tek kushtëzimi për një proces të besueshëm të zgjerimit të BE-së”. Diskutimi u fokusua në atë se si procesi i zgjerimit mund t’u japë peshë reale standardeve demokratike dhe pjesëmarrjes së shoqërisë civile.

Puka theksoi se vendet e rajonit tashmë kanë shumë prej mekanizmave formalë për pjesëmarrje, ndërsa sfida qëndron te ajo se çfarë ndodh kur këto mekanizma nuk prodhojnë pjesëmarrje dhe ndikim real. Ai vuri në dukje se shumë prej tyre janë ndërtuar nën shtysën e procesit të integrimit evropian dhe se, me dobësimin e kësaj shtyse, po bëhet gjithnjë më i dukshëm hendeku ndërmjet ekzistencës së mekanizmave dhe substancës së tyre.

Sipas tij, kjo kërkon veprim në dy drejtime. Në afat të shkurtër, rikthimin e peshës së kritereve demokratike dhe të pjesëmarrjes në procesin e zgjerimit. Në afat të gjatë, ndërtimin e një baze shoqërore që e bën pjesëmarrjen të qëndrueshme edhe përtej stimujve të jashtëm. In September 2026, Ansar Allah, commonly known as the Houthi movement, rapidly expanded its control over Yemen’s western coast. After capturing the port of Mocha on 10 September, the Houthis extended their control the following day to Mayyun (or Perim Island), Dhubab, the Hanish Islands, and six districts in Taiz and Hodeidah governorates, covering approximately 5,400 square kilometres. The operation began on 3 September with diversionary attacks against government forces advancing toward Sana’a. After government forces captured Hais on 5 September, the Houthis advanced south along the coast, forcing a withdrawal to avoid encirclement.

This expansion strengthens the Houthis’ ability to influence maritime traffic through Bab al-Mandeb and potentially use it to pressure Yemen’s internationally recognised government and Saudi Arabia. They could seek the removal of restrictions on air traffic at Sana’a airport and maritime movement through Hodeidah, as well as an end to Saudi support for government forces. Control of the coast also strengthens the Houthis’ position within Iran’s Axis of Resistance, since the territory provides greater protection for Iranian maritime deliveries of weapons, equipment and military expertise.

How Can the Mashriq Overcome Its Escalating Security Disorder?

发布源: Al Jazeera Centre for Studies (AJCS) --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Mashriq has entered an unprecedented period of security disorder. Earlier crises generally involved disputes over regimes, rivalry between neighbouring states, or limited Arab-Israeli wars. The current crisis is broader, combining Israel’s war against the Palestinians and other regional actors, interstate conflicts and competing struggles for influence. The escalation of the Yemeni conflict and the Houthi seizure of Bab al-Mandab, followed by attacks on Saudi Arabia, represents both a manifestation and a peak of this disorder.

This crisis must be understood against the background of the American security role in the Middle East. After the Second World War, following France’s withdrawal from Syria and Lebanon and Britain’s retreat from east of Suez, the United States assumed primary responsibility for regional security. After the Cold War, the American security umbrella had no serious competitor across most of the Mashriq apart from Iran. The American response to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia was therefore significant: President Trump’s reluctance to promise assistance raised doubts about the reliability of the American alliance.

The latest phase began with 7 October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. Israel responded with a devastating campaign in Gaza and expanded operations in the West Bank. item.content:encoded:
Government debt dynamics in the EU after the pandemic: the role of the snowball effect

发布源: 66. Institute of Public Finance (IJF) --Croatia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Institute of Public Finance will organize a virtual presentation onNovember 12, 2026, from 10:00 to 11:00 am (CET)based on anarticlepublished inPublic Sector Economics.

Mislav Brkić(Croatian National Bank) will present findings from his research analysing fiscal developments and the factors behind the decline in government debt ratios in EU member states after the pandemic, with a focus on the role of primary surpluses and the snowball effect. The results suggest that the favourable snowball effect, which reflects a positive difference between nominal growth rates and average interest rates on government debt, was the key factor behind the favourable dynamics of the debt ratio.

The presentation is open to the general public, but participants are required to register in advance at thisregistration link.

The anniversary comes at a time when public finances in Europe and around the world are facing complex fiscal pressures. Growing economic uncertainty, high public debt, population ageing and geopolitical shifts, alongside the demands of the green transition and rapid digital transformation, pose a challenge for governments seeking to reconcile fiscal sustainability with investment in economic growth, the quality of public services and social cohesion.

item.content:encoded:
A policy brief on the foreign policy of the Babiš government

发布源: 68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The return of the ANO movement to government at the end of 2025 –this time in coalition with Freedom and Direct Democracy (SPD) and Motorists for Themselves – raised a number of questions among Czechia’s international partners and allies. Concerns centered primarily on the country’s future stance on Ukraine, its role in the European Union, and the fulfillment of its NATO commitments. Although the new government declared a sharp break with the policies of the previous cabinet, reality presents a more nuanced picture. The first year in office reveals a blend of substantive and rhetorical shifts alongside continuity with the preceding period.

This policy brief uncovers the underlying motivations of key political actors and the dynamics shaping their relationships. It outlines how the differing priorities of the governing parties, the President, the parliamentary opposition, as well as the private sector and civil service intersect. The second part focuses on the outlook for the future: identifying areas where a stable course in Czech foreign policy can be expected, while highlighting issues whose development remains uncertain in today’s dynamic environment and warrants closer attention.

item.title: [Sadeq Institute --Libya] United States: A Chance for Improvement?
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
United States: A Chance for Improvement?

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Photo CreditFlickr

Libyan-American relations have always been contentious. After a period of good relations following American support for Libyan independence in 1951 and the short monarchical period, since the 1970s, belligerent confrontations and periods of strong tension have characterized this relationship with the regime of Gaddafi. In 1986, the U.S. President Ronald Reagan ordered a series of airstrikes on Tripoli and Benghazi that led to more than 40 casualties. The strikes were in retaliation to a bombing that occurred at a West Berlin discotheque, a frequently attended nightclub by U.S. soldiers, which the U.S. accused Libya of orchestrating. The situation further deteriorated during the later part of the 1980s, when Pan Am Flight 103, a transatlantic flight from London to New York, was bombed mid-air. Relations grew more strained as, what is known as the Lockerbie bombing, which left 270 dead, became the subject of an international investigation led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Subsequently, after the FBI found Libya to be the main culprit behind the Pan Am Flight attack, the U.S. placed Libya under heavy sanctions through the United Nations Security Council, a move which set the two countries at even greater odds. These violent outbursts laid the foundation for fraught relations between the two countries for the following ten years at least.

item.title: [Sadeq Institute --Libya] United Kingdom: Navigating Uncertainty
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
United Kingdom: Navigating Uncertainty

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Photo CreditCustos Group

History is important across the Middle East and North Africa and Libya is no exception. The graves of over 10,000 British soldiers, airmen and sailors in Tripoli, Benghazi and Tobruk pay testament to the British military’s role in the Second World War in North Africa. And the fact that those cemeteries are beautifully preserved and respected also pays testament to the lasting memories for Libyans of the sacrifices made by the British during that conflict.

Historical ties between the two nations endured following the establishment of the Kingdom of Libya when Libya won its independence on 24 December 1951. The United Kingdom supported the Libyan state during this period when oil revenues were low and the administration of the country needed support.

That relationship collapsed in 1969 when Gaddafi came to power in a bloodless coup. Despite spending 9 months of military training in England, Gaddafi had no affection for Britain. He moved quickly to demand the removal of British (and American) military bases, nationalized the hydrocarbon concessions of British Petroleum and withdrew approximately 550 million U.S. Dollars invested in British banks. Gaddafi’s association with Soviet Russia and support for Arab nationalism also conflicted with British policy during the Cold War.

item.title: [Sadeq Institute --Libya] Italy: In Pursuit of a New Role
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Italy: In Pursuit of a New Role

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Photo CreditFarnesina Digital Art Experience

Italy has a long and complex history and relationship to Libya that predates the events of the past decade. Italy is conscious of this history and on February 17th 2011 unlike it’s European neighbours in France and the United Kingdom expressed deep concerns regarding Libya’s future. This is largely as a result of the pre 2011 revival of ties between the two countries.

The 2008Treaty on Friendship Partnership and Cooperation between Italy and Libya- also known as the Benghazi Treaty - signed between Libya’s former leader Mu‘ammar Gaddafi and former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, aimed to put an end to the long dispute regarding Italy’s colonial legacy in Libya and to open a new chapter of strategic cooperation. Libya and Italy, by signing the treaty, intensified their bilateral relationship in terms of state investments and countering illegal migration from Libya to Italy’s shores. Italy, from its side, pledged to pay5 billion Eurosof reparations to its former colony for 32 years of occupation, to be invested in basic infrastructures.

Central and Eastern European China Policy Audit 2025–2026: Between De-Risking and Re-Engagement

发布源: 68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

China policy in Central and Eastern Europe is becoming harder to describe in terms of a simple divide between “pro-China” and “anti-China” governments. Russia’s war against Ukraine, China’s growing alignment with Moscow, uncertainty over US policy, domestic political changes, and differing levels of economic exposure to China are pushing governments in different directions.

While some countries are tightening their approach and treating China primarily as a security challenge, others are maintaining pragmatic economic ties or actively seeking closer political and commercial engagement. The result is not regional convergence, but growing divergence – with China’s political importance changing faster in many countries than the underlying economic relationship.

The first Central and Eastern European China Policy Audit 2025–2026 maps these different trajectories across the region, covering developments from January 2025 to July 2026. It identifies five broad policy approaches – security-first skeptics, managed pragmatists, a transition case, political openers, and structurally constrained actors – while emphasizing that these are fluid political logics rather than fixed alignments. The audit shows that the key question is no longer whether a country is “for” or “against” China, but what role governments believe Beijing can play in their security, economic development, and broader foreign-policy strategy.

China Observers in Central and Eastern Europe (CHOICE)

The Levant and Iraq Forum

The Levant and Iraq have long stood as the cradle of civilisation, enriched by deep-rooted diversity and a shared cultural heritage. Yet today, the region faces deep fragmentation, protracted conflicts, fragile states, and economic underdevelopment. To move forward, a shift from reactive policies to a collaborative, forward-looking vision is essential.

The Levant and Iraq Forum (LIF),launched on 30 October 2024during the MERI Forum in Erbil, is a timely response to this need. Formed by a consortium of regional think tanks, LIF seeks to foster cooperation, shape policy, and build regional resilience through shared research and dialogue.

As agrowing networkof think tanks and policy institutions, LIF connects policymakers, researchers, civil society, and international partners. It promotes evidence-based policymaking, inclusive strategies, and cross-border collaboration.

LIF’s missionis to empower communities, strengthen regional integration, and promote peaceful coexistence by identifying shared values and addressing common challenges. With rotating leadership and national coordinators, it operates on principles of autonomy and solidarity. Through annual forums and digital platforms, LIF amplifies collective impact and deepens regional cooperation.

A district office may know that applications take too long to process without knowing where the delay begins. A programme team may report activities every quarter but struggle to show whether services have improved. When we consider public sector management courses at the Ethiopian Economics Association, those are the questions that matter. A useful training decision starts with an actionable problem, rather than attendance alone.

Begin by naming a decision that a manager must make soon. Perhaps a department needs to prioritise inspections, distribute an operating budget or change the way it handles requests. Specify who makes that decision, what choices are available and what information is missing. A course on leadership may sound relevant, but the immediate gap might be interpreting service records.

An analyst may need to clean an administrative dataset. A supervisor may need to question the definition of an indicator. A director may need to decide what evidence justifies a change in spending. A shared course may miss these differences.

For us,policy-analysis trainingshould begin with the decisions managers need to make, rather than a promised certificate or a course title. We would ask a team to describe the decision in one sentence before comparing providers.

A good harvest report cannot tell us whether every household can afford food. A market price series may show a rise without revealing which families have lost income or access to markets. For food security research in Ethiopia, we favour a district evidence brief that brings these different observations together and makes their limits visible. It must never disguise uncertain estimates as a confirmed assessment of hunger in a specific woreda.

Start with a boundary, a period and a decision. Name the woreda or other administrative area, identify the months covered and describe the groups whose circumstances the brief can reasonably represent. A household survey from one cluster should not silently stand for an entire district.

The decision could concern the timing of a market assessment, the need to investigate declining purchasing power or the quality of an early warning signal. State who will use the brief and what action the available evidence could inform. This keeps the brief focused.

Separate a description of conditions during the observation period from a forecast. A current price, an earlier household survey and a projection for the next growing season belong in different columns. Record dates before comparing them.

Farm Productivity Data

发布源: Ethiopian Economics Association (EEA) --Ethiopia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Ethiopian Economics Association (EEA) was established as a non-profit making, non-political and non-religious..

A larger national harvest may reflect more land under cultivation, better yields on existing fields or both. In research on agricultural productivity in Ethiopia, we need to identify which result the evidence actually supports. A single annual average can hide variation between crops, locations and growing seasons. Our aim is to make comparisons useful without treating a headline figure as proof of improvement everywhere.

Total production measures the quantity harvested. Harvested area describes the land from which that output came. Yield relates the two: yield = harvested output ÷ harvested area, using matching units and the same crop and period. Wheat tonnes per harvested hectare, for example, should not be compared directly with the total tonnage of mixed cereals.

Farm outcomes extend beyond a yield measure. Income depends on output prices and production costs, among other factors. A family may report a higher yield yet face higher costs for hired labour or inputs. Resilience raises another question: whether production and household resources can withstand a difficult season. Each claim requires its own indicator.

Why Lebanon needs a broader security strategy

Lebanon's overlapping crises and renewed conflict have underscored the need for a national security strategy that addresses the multiple dimensions of insecurity facing the country and its population. Yet the security debate has largely centered on weapons and the extension of state authority.

While fundamental, these issues need to be situated within a strategy that assesses how different sources of insecurity interact, establi

shes priorities, clarifies institutional responsibilities, and identifies the military, diplomatic, political, economic, and social measures needed to provide meaningful protection.

The March 2026 escalation has made this task more urgent. Renewed conflict between Israel and Hezbollah has caused widespread destruction, including of entire villages, and mass displacement, while continued occupation and attacks have left many communities facing profound insecurity and uncertain prospects for return and recovery.

The conflict has also underscored the consequences of military decisions taken outside state institutions. Addressing Hezbollah's autonomous military role is therefore essential, but how this is achieved must form part of a broader strategy for national defense and civilian protection.

Establishing Lebanon’s National Commission for the Missing and Forcibly Disappeared

Fifty-one years since the outbreak of the 1975-90 war, Lebanon continues to grapple with unresolved legacies of conflict, including transitional justice, truth and reconciliation, and collective healing, particularly for the families of the missing and forcibly disappeared.

In the decades since the end of the war, the country has made some progress on this issue, such as the establishment of the National Commission for the Missing and Forcibly Disappeared. Yet, significant institutional, legal, and political challenges remain, compounded by limited public awareness, fragmented knowledge, and fading memories.

It is in this context that the Lebanese Center for Policy Studies (LCPS) is launching a series of papers addressing the issue of the missing and forcibly disappeared, focusing on themes related to “Dealing with the Past.” Through this endeavor, LCPS aims to inform policymakers, raise awareness, and advance practical solutions, with a particular emphasis on conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and social justice.

Fiscal Transparency in Lebanon: A Pathway to Stronger Governance

发布源: Lebanese Center for Policy Studies (LCPS) --Lebanon | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

In this policy brief, Nadine Merhi examines the key challenges undermining fiscal transparency in Lebanon, including weak implementation of existing laws, fragmented oversight institutions, limited access to reliable fiscal data, and low levels of citizen participation. The brief proposes short, medium, and long-term reforms to strengthen institutional capacity and coordination, improve digital infrastructure and public access to financial information, and enhance citizen engagement. These measures aim to reinforce accountability, improve governance, and restore public trust in state institutions.

The TradeCom II Programme, in partnership with REPOA, aims to strengthen the capacity of policymakers, exporters, and trade associations to assess and review trade policies. By promoting trade competitiveness and diversification, the programme expands trading opportunities within Tanzania, the EAC, and with the European Union (EU).

Strengthening REPOA in partnership with the International Institute of Social Studies of Erasmus University, Rotterdam (ISS) is pleased to launch a research and capacity building programme titledStrengthening Capacity of Exporters to Sustainably Enhance Export Competitiveness and Diversification.

This programme aims at strengthening the capacity of policymakers, exporters, and trade associations to assess and review trade and related economic policies to promote trade competitiveness and diversification for widening trading opportunities within Tanzania, EAC including with the EU. The initiative will enhance the formulation and implementation of suitable trade policies, including strategies for strategic measures to harness the opportunities arising from the effective implementation of regional and international trade agreements. item.content:encoded:
Disarming Resistance: The Trilateral Framework Agreement

发布源: Al-Shabaka: The Palestinian Policy Network --Palestine | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

On June 26, 2026, Lebanon, the US, and the Israeli regime signed aTrilateral Frameworkagainst the backdrop offierce military attackson Lebanon and the invasion of its south. This aggression was part of the broader US-Israeli regional assault that also devastatedIran, Syria, and Palestine, upending thegeopolitical order.

In this commentary, we speak with Al-Shabaka policy analyst Jaber Suleiman, who examines pivotal questions about this framework agreement and its implications for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon and the liberation struggle more broadly. He emphasizes the grave implications of this agreement, as it makes Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory conditional on the disarmament of Hezbollah, thereby holding the resistance factions and the Lebanese state responsible for ending the war and the occupation, while absolving Israel of accountability.

The framework agreement does not directly address Palestinians; it does so indirectly in relation to the disarmament of Hezbollah and nonstate groups, especially in Palestinian refugee camps. The broader context, however, is the 2023 war that began with the Israeli genocidal campaign in Gaza. This war has greatly impacted the situation of Palestinians in Lebanon, particularly since the start of theground offensiveinto Lebanon in October 2024.

In a moment of genocide, we have no revolutionary leadership at the helm of our struggle. This is, perhaps, one of the most painful truths we have to contend with in this chapter of our ongoing Nakba. This is our biggest and most urgent challenge as Palestinians. Resuscitating our struggle from the ashes of the past three decades, from the failures of partition and negotiations, and the ensuing horror of genocide and genocidal reconstruction. We are (re)building our revolution. We must.

The vacuum on the level of the leadership has not prevented the emergence of an expansive popular movement that has sustained our struggle. This movement is nurtured by a persistent, historical, and deeply revolutionary narrative that informs our everyday politics as Palestinians, and that transcends all the scripts imposed on us. It is a narrative that is grounded in our thawabet, the fixed principles that define our cause: namely the right of all refugees to return home; the right of self-determination in the whole of Palestine, with Jerusalem as our capital; and the right to resist in all forms necessary. L’initiative Prospective Agricole et Rurale (IPAR) a été suscitée par des spécialistes de l’agriculture et du monde rural qui appuyaient déjà les organisations paysannes et qui étaient intéressés par la création d’espaces permanents de réflexion prospective et stratégique.Cette initiative a été formalisée en 2005 par quatre institutions, deux publiques (DAPS et ISRA) et deux privées (CNCR et ENDA GRAF).Un protocole d’accord unit les initiateurs de l’IPAR. En août 2008, une assemblée générale constitutive a permis de faire évoluer l’IPAR à une association d’utilité publique, constituée de personnes physiques, pour garantir son autonomie d’action. Elle a adopté les statuts et le règlement intérieur et défini les organes de gouvernance de l’association.Elle est désormais reconnue par les autorités compétentes, sous le récépissé n°13615/MINT/DAGAT/DEL/AS. Prof A.T Simbine (nee Okoosi) (PhD, Ibadan) is a Professor of Political Science & InternationalRelations. She was appointed as NISER Director-General (DG) by President Muhammadu Buharion May 20, 2022. Her appointment took effect from June 1, 2022. Prof Simbine is the first woman to be appointed DG of Nigeria’s 62-year-old premiere Think Tank. Until herappointment as DG, she was Research Professor in the Political and Governance PolicyDepartment (PGPD) and Head, Knowledge Management Department (KMD), NISER.She started her career at NISER as a Youth Corps member in 1984 and rose to the rank of Research Professor in 2010. Her Research and consulting interests include – Public sector governance, the Legislature, Politics and Elections in Nigeria; Gender issues especially Women’s Education and Political Participation; International Relations; Peacekeeping and Conflict Resolution; as well as issues in socio-economic development and good governance.

item.title: [Arab Forum for Alternatives (AFA) --Egypt] Patterns of Interaction with Knowledge in the Arab Region
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Arab Forum for Alternatives (AFA) --Egypt官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Patterns of Interaction with Knowledge in the Arab Region

发布源: Arab Forum for Alternatives (AFA) --Egypt | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

How do those interested in acquiring knowledge across the Arab region engage with knowledge today, and why does this matter?

This regional project examines how knowledge is produced, circulated, and engaged with, this is across diverse Arab contexts. It seeks to understand the relationship between knowledge and its publics, exploring how ideas travel, who engages with them, and what shapes their influence.

Guided by the central question, “Who engages with what, how, where, and why?” the project investigates the conditions that enable knowledge to inform, mobilise, and resonate across different societies.

Methodology:This project adopts a mixed-methods approach, combining quantitative, qualitative, and content analysis.

This page will regularly share new findings, publications, and opportunities to engage.

Gouvernance démocratique en Côte d'Ivoire: les15révélations

发布源: Centre de Recherche et de Formation sur le Developpement Integre (CREFDI) --Côte d'IvoireThis link opens in a new window | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Gouvernance démocratique: 15 révélations des enquêtes d’Afrobarometer à découvrir sur le degré de satisfaction et les aspirations des Ivoiriens

Le président Alassane Ouattara a pris la décision de ne pas se présenter aux prochaines élections présidentielles prévues à la fin de l’année 2020. Si cette décision semble être bien apprécié par beaucoup d’acteurs de la communauté nationale et internationale qui y voient « une victoire de la démocratie », d’autres se montrent sceptiques au regard de la situation sur le respect des principes de bonne gouvernance et des manquements notés pour la préparation des prochaines joutes électorales.Ces 15 révélations des résultats de l’enquête d’Afrobarometer menée en novembre 2019 renseignent sur la situation de la démocratie et de l’État de droit en Côte d’Ivoire durant sa présidence telle que perçue par les Ivoiriens. L‘enquête a interviewé 1.200 adultes ivoiriens. Un échantillon de cette taille donne des résultats avec une marge d’erreur de +/-3% à un niveau de confiance de 95%.Ces perceptions sont autant importantes pour les acteurs non-étatiques, pour l’État que les candidats aspirant à des fonctions électives.

En résumé, ces résultats des enquêtes d’Afrobarometer montrent que beaucoup d’efforts doivent être consentis par les décideurs afin d’être en phase avec les aspirations des citoyens. item.title: [Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia] Counting Every Dollar
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Counting Every Dollar

发布源: Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

How transparent is Namibia’s national budget, and how effectively can citizens and Parliament hold government accountable for public spending?

This IPPR research paper examines budget transparency, public participation and parliamentary oversight, drawing on the latest Open Budget Survey findings. While Namibia has made progress in publishing budget information, significant weaknesses remain in public participation, legislative scrutiny and follow-up on audit findings.

The paper recommends stronger parliamentary oversight, more meaningful opportunities for citizen engagement and improved access to fiscal information. It also highlights the importance of transparent management of future revenues from Namibia’s oil, gas and mining sectors.

The research was supported by the Embassy of Ireland.

item.title: [Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia] Open Budget Survey: Namibia
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Open Budget Survey: Namibia

发布源: Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Open Budget Survey (OBS) 2025 assesses transparency, public participation and oversight in national budget processes across 82 countries. Namibia scores 53 out of 100 for budget transparency, 17 for public participation and 48 for oversight, highlighting continuing weaknesses in public access to budget information, opportunities for citizen engagement and parliamentary scrutiny of public finances.

The survey is produced by the International Budget Partnership (IBP). The IPPR completed the national assessment, contributing to an internationally comparable evidence base that helps track progress, identify gaps and advocate for greater accountability in the management of public resources.

The findings underline the need for more accessible budget information, stronger parliamentary oversight and meaningful public participation in decisions about how Namibia’s public money is spent.

item.content:encoded:
Green Hydrogen – Communities, People at the Centre

发布源: Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) --Namibia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

This edition of the IPPR’s Green Hydrogen Monitor focuses on “Communities, People at the Centre: What should benefit-sharing look like in a just transition?” Featuring perspectives from civil society, industry and government, it explores how Namibia can ensure that green hydrogen and related developments deliver meaningful, lasting benefits for local communities. Key issues include community participation, environmental accountability, equitable benefit-sharing and skills development. The central question is whether Namibia’s green transition will improve the lives of those most directly affected by it.

item.content:encoded:
Industries extractives

发布源: Center for Environment and Development --Cameroon | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

L’exploitation de l’or au Cameroun est aujourd’hui insuffisamment maîtrisée par l’État. En plus d’être un défi sectoriel relevant de l’administration minière, de la fiscalité ou de la protection de l’environnement

Une dissociation persistante entre les dynamiques d’investissement et les mécanismes de protection des droits et des moyens de subsistance des populations.

L’orpaillage artisanal et déforestation à l’Est du Cameroun accélèrent une crise écologique majeure, perturbant le climat et la sécurité alimentaire

Analyse détaillée des effets combinés de l’orpaillage artisanal et de la déforestation dans l’Est du Cameroun, soulignant leurs liens avec l’accélération de la crise climatique.

Le CED lance un appel à propositions sur l’extractivisme et les conflits écologiques au Cameroun, en vue du colloque APAD 2026

Annual Country Reports

发布源: 9. World Food Programme – Italy | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Annual Country Reports (ACRs) are key, annual accountability documents produced by country offices. They inform donors how their funds were used during the reporting year. They describe WFP’s performance story in an accurate, transparent and evidence-based manner, by assessing the effectiveness, efficiency and economy of our operations in the pursuit of zero hunger.

The ACRs fulfil a contractual agreement with donors and contribute to WFP’s annual corporate statistics and Annual Performance Report. The reports serve as a repository of institutional knowledge and are a key source of information for evaluations. The availability and quality of output and outcome data directly influences the evaluation conclusions on WFP interventions. ACRs thereby contribute to both objectives of "accountability" and "learning".

item.content:encoded:
How Expensive Fuel Could Shape Uganda’s Economy

发布源: Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

At UGX 7,000 per litre of diesel, and even higher in some parts of Uganda by November 2026, and with petrol also approaching UGX 7,000, rising fuel prices are a concern for everyone.

Farmers face higher costs of transporting produce, businesses are spending more on production and distribution, and households are paying more for essential goods. The bigger concern, however, is what persistently expensive fuel could mean for the economy tomorrow.

According to the Uganda Bureau of Statistics, annual petrol and diesel inflation reached 30.9 percent and 42.5 percent, respectively, in September 2026, while headline inflation increased from 4.1 percent in August to 4.6 percent. Persistent high fuel prices could intensify broader inflationary pressures.

Uganda remains vulnerable as a net importer of petroleum products, with domestic pump prices influenced by global oil prices, exchange-rate movements, transport costs and taxes. Recent shilling depreciation past UGX 4,000 per US dollar and the UGX 200 increase in fuel excise duty for FY2026/27 have further intensified price pressures.

Meanwhile, the US Energy Information Administration’s October outlook projected Brent crude oil averaging USD 105 per barrel in the final quarter of 2026, reflecting Middle East tensions that threaten oil supplies and shipping routes. Even if global prices stabilise, exchange-rate pressures and high-cost fuel stocks could delay relief for Ugandan consumers.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Is Uganda Ready for the Gen Z Labour Force?

发布源: Economic Policy Research Center (EPRC) --Uganda | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Imagine a young employee completing a report electronically, only to be told to print it, sign it, scan it and email it back. Somewhere between the printer and the scanner, so much is lost: innovation and time.

This imagined encounter captures a question Uganda must confront: is the country ready for Generation Z’s labour force? Welcoming young workers requires more than giving them a password and a motivational speech. It requires productive jobs, relevant skills and institutions willing to unlearn and learn.

Generation Z, alias Gen Z, broadly refers to people born from the late-1990s to around 2010. Belonging to the same generation does not mean having identical experiences or expectations. A young farmer in Nakaseke and a software developer in Kampala may be similar in age but face very different working realities. Understanding this generation therefore requires looking beyond fashionable labels and recognising differences in education, income, location and access to technology.

International evidence nevertheless offers useful insights into how many young people approach work. Deloitte’s 2026 survey, covering more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents across 44 countries, found that 74% of Gen Z respondents used artificial intelligence to some extent in their daily work. Only 6% identified achieving a leadership position as their primary career goal.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在4. Action Against Hunger – Spain官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Countries suffering the most from hunger

发布源: 4. Action Against Hunger – Spain | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Increasing conflict in Burkina Faso is driving up food prices, pushing thousands of people into food insecurity and more than 40,000 into famine.

Mali, which already had high levels of acute food insecurity, is experiencing an escalation of violent conflict, causing hunger to increase further. For the first time, thousands of people are suffering from "catastrophic" levels of hunger.

In South Sudan, widespread flooding, conflict and a weak economy may intensify the hunger crisis in the world's newest nation. An estimated 40,000 people are struggling to survive in famine conditions.

Between December 2023 and February 2024, at the height of the conflict, the entire population (about 2.2 million people) is estimated to be facing high levels of acute food insecurity, including more than half a million people in the most critical situation on the food insecurity scale.

item.title: [4. Action Against Hunger – Spain] Causes and consequences
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在4. Action Against Hunger – Spain官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Causes and consequences

发布源: 4. Action Against Hunger – Spain | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The planet produces enough food to feed all its inhabitants. However, more than 3 billion people cannot afford a healthy diet.

The interrelated problems of poverty, inequality, conflict, climate change, gender discrimination and weak government and health systems contribute to the lack of access to nutritious food for millions of families around the world.

When children don't have enough to eat, their brains and bodies suffer. This prevents them from growing, learning and working, i.e. from developing their full potential. Without treatment, severe hunger can kill many children.

But it doesn't have to be this way: hunger is predictable, preventable and treatable. With the right tools and policies, we can save the lives of undernourished children and help them get the nutritious food they need to thrive. We can create a world without hunger, for everyone, forever: first, we must tackle its root causes.

75% of the world's undernourished people live in conflict zones.

Extreme poverty, lack of sufficient food and hunger are closely linked.

The climate crisis is causing hunger and malnutrition around the world.

Emergencies disrupt and destroy livelihoods.

Approximately 3.1 billion people lack access to a healthy diet.

Each year, our life-saving and life-changing programmes reach 28 million people.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Infection After Surgery Abroad: Wound Signs, Resistant Bacteria and What Happens at Home

发布源: Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

PublishedOctober 22, 2026· Last reviewedOctober 27, 2026

An infection after surgery abroad most often shows up at home: a surgical wound infection can start from about 2 to 3 days after the operation until the wound heals, usually 2 to 3 weeks, so the warning signs, red, hot, swollen or weeping skin, pus, a wound that opens or a fever, need acting on wherever you are, and if you are admitted to a UK hospital within the next year, expect to be screened for resistant bacteria because you were a hospital patient abroad.None of that is a reason not to go. It is a reason to know the signs, bring the right paperwork and treat the first weeks home as part of the operation.

I get more emails about this than almost anything else that happens after people fly back. Usually it is a photo of a wound and a question about whether it looks right. I am not the person to answer that, and nor is a forum. The useful thing I can do is set out what normal looks like, what does not, and what the system at home will do.

Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust describes a surgical wound infection as germs getting into the cut made during an operation, most often a skin infection that can sometimes spread deeper1. They are not common, but they can occur from 2 to 3 days after surgery until the wound has healed, which is usually 2 to 3 weeks, and occasionally several months later. Operations on parts of the body with lots of germs, such as the gut, carry a higher chance.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
What to Pack for Surgery in Thailand: Documents, Medicines, Clothes and the Trip Home

发布源: Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

PublishedOctober 28, 2026· Last reviewedNovember 2, 2026

Packing for surgery in Thailand comes down to four things: the paperwork in your hand luggage, your regular medicines in their original packaging with a prescription copy, loose recovery clothes that need no lifting or bending to put on, and a case light enough that you never have to lift it yourself on the way home.Everything else is optional. The mistake I see most is people packing for a holiday with an operation in the middle, when the operation should decide the bag.

Most of the trouble I have watched people get into with luggage was at the end of the trip, not the start. One reader had a beautifully organised folder on the way out and came home with her discharge notes stuffed in a hotel laundry bag in the hold, which is exactly where they were not when her GP asked to see them the week after.

Carry every document you need in your hand luggage, on paper, with photos of each on your phone. If your case goes missing for three days, the operation should not.

The UK government’s advice notes that all hospitals in Thailand require a guarantee of payment before treating patients2, which is one more reason the payment arrangements should be settled and written down before you go.

item.title: [Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand] Hernia Repair in Thailand: Keyhole or Open, How Long to Stay, and the Flight Home
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Hernia Repair in Thailand: Keyhole or Open, How Long to Stay, and the Flight Home

发布源: Institute of Security and International Studies (ISIS) --Thailand | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

PublishedOctober 16, 2026· Last reviewedOctober 21, 2026

Inguinal hernia repair is usually a day case, done either by keyhole surgery through a few small cuts or by open surgery through one cut in the groin, normally with a mesh, and most people go home the same day; what makes it manageable abroad is the short hospital stay, and what makes it tricky is the 4 to 6 weeks of no heavy lifting that overlaps with suitcases, transfers and a long-haul flight.It is one of the operations people most often ask me about, because it is common, the waiting lists at home can be long, and it sounds simple. Mostly it is. The parts that go wrong for travellers are the logistics around it, not the surgery itself.

A friend of a reader had his repair in Bangkok last year and was back walking around the hotel garden the next afternoon. What caught him out was the airport. He had planned the flight for day six, which his surgeon was happy with, and had not thought at all about who would lift his case off the belt at the other end.

The NHS describes two main ways of repairing an inguinal hernia: laparoscopic (keyhole) surgery with a few small cuts in the tummy, and open surgery with one larger cut in the groin1. In both, a thin sheet of mesh is usually placed over the weak spot and fixed with small stitches, though sometimes stitches alone are used. 发布源: Social Policy and Development Centre (SPDC) --Pakistan | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

This revised report updates the Jordan 2024 cigarette tax simulation, incorporating new demographic inputs, improved elasticity estimates, and modernized mortality modeling. The study evaluates four excise tax scenarios and demonstrates how well‑designed reforms can simultaneously strengthen government revenue and reduce smoking prevalence. Among the options, a combined increase in both specific and tiered excise components delivers the strongest impact – raising revenue, curbing consumption, and averting thousands of premature deaths.

发布源: Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) --Bangladesh | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

National vision is a prime component in development planning for any country across the world. It serves as an important benchmark for measuring the performance of a government and ensuring that it becomes accountable to the citizens. Today, all the major political parties of Bangladesh, including ruling Awami League and political opposition BNP, have their own political vision with regard to the future of Bangladesh. The very notion of drawing a long-term plan for a balanced growth and development of the country has brought a significant change in the history of Bangladesh.

However, crafting a national or political vision to set the future course of actions concerning the country’s development is relatively new in Bangladesh. Until 2007, the political parties did not have any defined vision or long-term plan on where they want to see the country in future.

The Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), Bangladesh’s premier civil society think-tank, played a catalytic role in this matter through civic activism. This had been particularly pronounced in the wake of national elections in an effort to articulate development agendas for the newly elected governments.  National Policy Forum (2001) and National Policy Review Forum (2003) are examples of such actions. Strategic Priorities and Policies on Wednesday, 23 September 2026

Roundtable on Strengthening

Bangladesh’s National Security Architecture: Strategic Priorities and Policies

The Bangladesh Institute of

International and Strategic Studies (BIISS), in collaboration with the British

High Commission, Dhaka, organised a roundtable titled “Strengthening

Bangladesh’s National Security Architecture: Strategic Priorities and Policies”

on Wednesday, 23 September 2026.

The roundtable brought together

policymakers, security and defence experts, academics, researchers and other

relevant stakeholders to exchange views on Bangladesh’s evolving national

security landscape and the strategic priorities required to strengthen the

country’s national security architecture.

The discussions focused on

contemporary and emerging security challenges facing Bangladesh, institutional

coordination, strategic policymaking, and the need for a comprehensive and

forward-looking approach to national security. Participants also exchanged

views on strengthening institutional capacity, enhancing coordination among

relevant stakeholders, and developing effective policy responses to emerging

traditional and non-traditional security challenges.

The roundtable provided an

important platform for informed and constructive dialogue on Bangladesh’s

national security priorities and contributed to broader discussions on

developing a resilient, coordinated and effective national security

architecture.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) --Bangladesh官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Dialogue Promoting Inclusive Society

发布源: Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) --Bangladesh | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

‘Dialogue’ is a collective way of opening up judgments and assumptions – which allows people to understand others’ viewpoints. It is a platform to frame a problem and look for options collectively to solve it. Dialogue is also a process that weaves threads of understanding between groups that naturally helps to reduce misunderstandings, conflict, and tension and therefore to dissolve problems.

Today, dialogues have become commonplace as it created a public sphere in the society. People nowadays actively engage themselves in dialogues and in this process new ideas and collective wisdom arise. In Bangladesh, the practice of holding dialogues has become far more widespread and not a single day goes by without a TV talk-show, which is also a form of dialogue, being held on one topic or another. The governments, NGOs, mass media and think tanks in the region now follow the dialogic culture.

However, the situation was not the same in the 90s that witnessed a dramatic escalation in the globalisation trend, particularly for the emerging market economies. Only a few civil society members and orgnisations in Bangladesh used to organise seminars in that time and that too was done only on an occasional basis. In the era of growing economic reformation, they felt the urgency for a common platform to understand the rapid changes happening around the world as well as in Bangladesh, and to contribute to the change to establish a participatory development process. item.content:encoded:
Strategic Plan 2026-2030

发布源: Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) --Philippines | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

PIDS is a nonstock, nonprofit, government research institution engaged in long-term, policy-oriented research. It was established on September 26, 1977 by virtue of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1201 as an agency attached to the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA), the Philippine government's socioeconomic planning arm, for policy and program coordination.

It was created to serve as an effective means of bridging the gap between public policy formulation and research. Given the orientation and character of pure academic research, it was the government's goal to establish a national research institution that will perform policy-oriented research on all aspects of the Philippine economy and assist the government in formulating plans and policies that are evidence based and fully responsive to the requirements of national planning and policymaking for national development.

《問題と研究》團隊合影。（左起為石原忠浩、井上園子編輯助理）

四本期刊團隊於會議中進行熱烈的討論。

政大驕傲X國關光榮—臺灣最早、最具權威的政治學門期刊

政大國際關係研究中心（國關中心）是全臺灣最早出版政治學門期刊的單位，每年常態性經營四份重要期刊，包含：《問題與研究》、《中國大陸研究》、《Issues & Studies》、《問題と研究》等。國關中心為了擴大期刊影響力，特別於2025年8月25日召開了四份期刊的編輯聯合工作會議，由國關中心王信賢主任主持，與陳至潔副主任、林義鈞副主任、王韻副研究員、石原忠浩副研究員，與政大外交系張文揚教授，以及四位編輯助理，一同為下半年度及未來的願景進行討論和決策。

在此次的會議中，王信賢主任強調國關中心出版的四份期刊是政治大學的驕傲、國關中心的光榮，原因是政大國關中心於1956年創刊了臺灣最早的政治學期刊—《問題與研究》，並且在1960年代陸續發行了《匪情月報（後改成：《中國大陸研究》）》、《Issues & Studies》、《問題と研究》等國關中心刊物，不曾間斷。同時，國關中心刊物成功的公開發行過程，更在1970年代之後成為其它新興的台灣政治學學術期刊的效法對象。近期，國關中心刊物除了持續被收錄於重要學術期刊資料庫外，更屢次獲得國家圖書館、華藝Airiti Library的傳播獎項榮耀。政大國關中心除了與有榮焉之外，更深刻感受上述四大刊物的永續經營是任重道遠的任務。因此，編輯聯合工作會議決議，國關中心四份期刊將常態性地與臺灣重要政治學門學會、年會合作，持續推廣刊物影響力。其次，四份期刊也將透過後年（2027）國立政治大學100週年校慶活動，強化期刊榮耀與政大歷史的結合，彰顯國關中心的特殊貢獻。

《問題與研究》是華文世界首份研究國際關係、區域研究、國際發展、政治經濟學等全球性議題的刊物；《中國大陸研究》是臺灣及華人世界第一本從社會科學的角度，探討中國大陸各領域發展的刊物；《Issues & Studies》則為臺灣首份以英文出版的政治學期刊，致力於探討臺灣、中國和東亞國內和國際事務相關議題；《問題と研究》是臺灣唯一以日文出版的學術期刊，收錄內容包括中國研究與亞太研究。四份期刊皆為每年3、6、9、12月出刊，《問題與研究》及《中國大陸研究》持續收錄於TSSCI學術期刊資料庫，《Issues & Studies》收錄於Scopus、ESCI等國際期刊資料庫，《問題と研究》則收錄於華藝Airiti Library。

在會議的尾聲，王信賢主任歡迎大家隨時掌握國關中心的最新消息，未來四本期刊也會秉持高標準的學術精神，持續出版優質學術作品；同時，也歡迎有志之士踴躍投稿，共同參與榮耀。

《問題與研究》季刊http://wenti.nccu.edu.tw/《中國大陸研究》http://mcs.nccu.edu.tw/index.html《Issues&Studies》http://issues.nccu.edu.tw/《問題と研究》http://iirj.nccu.edu.tw/index.html

item.content:encoded:
Former Executive Director

发布源: Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka (IPS) --Sri Lanka | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Saman Kelegama was the Executive Director of the Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka (IPS) from 1995 until his sudden demise in 2017. He was a trade policy economist who also worked on industrial economics, public enterprise reform, and macroeconomics.

He obtained his D.Phil (Econ) from Oxford University, UK in 1990, with an MSc (Econ) from Oxford University and an MSc (Maths) first class degree from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur, India.

He was a Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences of Sri Lanka and the Sri Lanka Economic Association. He was a Visiting Fellow at the Australia South Asia Research Centre, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia (1998); Salzburg Fellow (1997); USIS International Visitor (1993); and Visiting Fellow, Institute of Social Studies, The Hague, The Netherlands (1992/3). He was a Visiting Lecturer at the University of Colombo, Post-Graduate Institute of Management (PIM), Sri Lanka, Bandaranaike Diplomatic Training Institute (BDTI), Sri Lanka and several other institutions. He served as a consultant to the World Bank, ADB, UNDP, UNIDO, ILO, UN-ESCAP, Commonwealth Secretariat, among other organisations.

Dr. Kelegama also served in the Board of Directors of many government, private sector and professional institutions, as well as in the governing boards of a number of regional and international institutions. Our vision is for a resilient Pacific region of peace, harmony, security, social inclusion and prosperity, that ensures all Pacific peoples can lead free, healthy and productive lives.

It requires a long-term vision and a carefully considered regional strategy that reinforces commitment and working together to leverage our collective strengths and build a better future for our people.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在New Economic School (NESG) --Georgia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Why Do We Need Art and Morality?

发布源: New Economic School (NESG) --Georgia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Why Do We Need Art and Morality?ℹ️ Join us for the objectivist discussion on Saturday, September 21, 2024 from 12:00 PM to 14:00 PM.

ℹ️ This exciting event, hosted by the New Economic School - Georgia, University of Georgia, School Clubs Associacion and High School of Georgia.

Modern art has become a circus of absurdity, with bananas taped to walls selling for millions, while art’s true purpose is lost in mysticism. But art is far more than a joke—it’s a reflection of human values and greatness. In this engaging talk, we’ll reveal how art has drifted into chaos and lost its meaning.If we want to build a better future, we need to de-mystify art and reclaim it as a celebration of beauty and human flourishing. Join us, to discover why embracing real art is essential for achieving a culture where life can truly thrive.What would you think if someone told you that morality is not about sacrifice? If he told you that you need it to get the most out of your personal life? If he told you that it is a necessity for the survival of human beings?That's exactly what Ayn Rand argues. Join us on Saturday to explore her revolutionary ideas about morality and human life.ℹ️ Topics will be led by guest experts:➡️ Itamar Feldman;➡️ Yonatan Daon;Yonatan Daon is an Israeli activist, art historian, and blogger, dedicated to promoting Objectivist philosophy and connecting with audiences worldwide.ℹ️ Attendance is freeℹ️ Registration link:https://forms.gle/z3m7bf77gyJ9h2NP7

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
When Grievances Go Viral: Digital Media and Nepal’s Changing Democracy

发布源: Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Nepal’s Gen Z protests revealed more than the organizing power of social media. They showed that digital platforms have become places where people practice citizenship. People encounter public issues, compare experiences, question authority, and decide whether to act through these platforms. For Nepal, the democratic challenge is clear: how can the energy of rapid online mobilization be converted into informed, inclusive, and sustained participation?

In early September 2025, following an official registration deadline, the government directed the Nepal Telecommunications Authority (NTA) to deactivate unregistered social media platforms. The restrictions became an immediate trigger for the Gen Z demonstrations that began at Maitighar in Kathmandu on September 8 and developed into a nationwide political crisis. The movement also expressed deeper anger over corruption, political exclusion, lack of transparency, and weak public accountability.

From private frustration to public action

Collective action begins when people discover that a private difficulty is widely shared. A young Nepali may experience unemployment, an unfair recruitment process, or poor public services as a personal setback. When similar accounts appear repeatedly in videos, memes, and posts, the problem acquires a public meaning. “My frustration” becomes “our condition.”

Social media accelerates this change. Likes, comments, and shares offer visible evidence that others recognize the same problem. Messaging gro

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Case for Terrain-Smart Agricultural Policy in Nepal

发布源: Nepal Economic Forum (NEF) --Nepal | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Walk through a hill village in Gorkha or Baitadi during planting season, and you will notice something: fewer hands in the fields than there used to be. A son is in Qatar, a daughter-in-law is in Kuwait, and the previously double-cropped terraces are now planted once, if at all. The house has a new tin roof and a motorcycle parked outside, paid for by money wired home every month. But the fields around it are quietly doing less than they used to.

This is the story most people tell about Nepal’s two biggest economic facts sitting side by side. Remittances make up more than aquarterof the country’s entire economy, among the highest shares anywhere in the world. Agriculture, meanwhile, stillemploysmore than six in ten workers, and yet its productivity has barely moved in years. The obvious explanation is that migration hollowed out the farms, the workers left, thus the yields fell.

I wanted to know if that story actually holds up once you look at the whole country, district by district, rather than just at the villages where it’s most visible.

Building a fuller picture

Using government census data onmigration and labor, matched with the agriculture ministry’s district-levelcrop data, I compared 75 districts within Nepal in the dataset on two things: how migration-dependent each district is, and how its cereal yields compare to the national picture. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Civil Society Institute (CSI) --Armenia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Հայաստան․ Նազելի Վարդանյանի և Թեհմինե Ենոքյանի՝ կին բնապահպան իրավապաշտպանների նկատմամբ դատական հետապնդումների վերսկսում

发布源: Civil Society Institute (CSI) --Armenia | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Մարդու իրավունքների միջազգային ֆեդերացիան (FIDH) և Խոշտանգումների դեմ համաշխարհային կազմակերպությունը (OMCT)՝ իրենց համատեղՄարդու իրավունքների պաշտպանների պաշտպանության դիտորդական կենտրոնի (The Observatory for the Protection of Human Rights Defenders)շրջանակում, «Քաղաքացիական հասարակության ինստիտուտ» ՀԿ-ի (ՔՀԻ) հետ համատեղ, լուրջ մտահոգություն են հայտնում «Լիդիան Արմենիա» հանքարդյունաբերական ընկերության կողմից կին բնապահպան իրավապաշտպաններ Նազելի Վարդանյանի և Թեհմինե Ենոքյանի դեմ նախաձեռնված նոր դատական վարույթների կապակցությամբ։

Փարիզ, Ժնև, Երևան, 9 հոկտեմբերի 2026 թ.— Ստորագրող կազմակերպությունները մտահոգված են, որ այս դատական վարույթները, նույն իրավապաշտպանների դեմ նախկինում իրականացված դատական գործընթացների համատեքստում դիտարկվելիս, ունեն հանրային մասնակցության դեմ ուղղված ռազմավարական հայցերին (SLAPP) բնորոշ հատկանիշներ և կարող են զսպող ազդեցություն ունենալ Հայաստանում բնապահպանական իրավապաշտպան գործունեության և հանրային շահին վերաբերող քննարկումների վրա։

Դիտորդական կենտրոնըև ՔՀԻ-ն կոչ են անում վերջ տալ դատական վարույթների այնպիսի կիրառմանը, որը կարող է վախեցնել, լռեցնել կամ հետ պահել բնապահպան իրավապաշտպաններին և հանրային վերահսկողություն իրականացնող այլ անձանց ու կազմակերպություններին հանրային կարևորություն ունեցող հարցերի վերաբերյալ բարձրաձայնելուց։

Նազելի Վարդանյանըիրավաբան և երկարամյա բնապահպան իրավապաշտպան է, ինչպես նաև «Հայաստանի անտառներ» ՀԿ-ի ղեկավարը։ Նա երկար տարիներ ակտիվորեն զբաղվում է Ամուլսարի ոսկու հանքի և դրա բնապահպանական, սոցիալական ու մարդու իրավունքն

item.content:encoded:
CIRDAP Vision, Mission, Values, Functions

发布源: Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and the Pacific (CIRDAP) --Bangladesh | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

The Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and the Pacific (CIRDAP) is a regional, intergovernmental and autonomous organisation. It was established on 6 July 1979 at the initiative of the countries of the Asia-Pacific region and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations with support from several other UN bodies and donors. The Centre came into being to meet the felt needs of the developing countries at that time as an institution for promoting integrated rural development in the region.

From the original six members, CIRDAP has now grown up as a Centre of 15 member countries. The member-countries are Afghanistan, Bangladesh (Host State), Fiji, India, Indonesia, IR Iran, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand and Vietnam.

Operating through designated contact ministries and link institutions in member countries, CIRDAP promotes regional cooperation. It plays a supplementary and reinforcing role in supporting and furthering the effectiveness of integrated rural development programmes in Asia and the Pacific.

To be a Centre of Excellence & multi-level platform for cooperation in knowledge transfer and capacity building for developing countries in integrated rural affairs for sustainable development in Asia and the Pacific Region.

The objectives of the Centre are:

* To assist national action and promote regional co-operation relating to Integrated Rural Development (IRD), in the region

CURRENT AND PREVIOUS RESEARCH FELLOWS

Visiting Research Fellow

September 2017 - July 2018

Abhi Goyal is a Fulbright Student Researcher from the United States, focused on the topic of informal communities and people who migrate in urban areas of the Kyrgyz Republic.

Informal communities are generally not included in demographic data about the Kyrgyz Republic, preventing organizations and the government from creating policies adapted to their situations. Abhi’s research focuses on the reason for these communities’ creation, their place in migration patterns, and their composition.

Before this research, Abhi worked at the USAID-funded Strengthening Results, Partnerships, and Innovations in Nutrition Globally (SPRING) Project, writing a social media strategy to reach urban households in the Kyrgyz Republic with nutrition information, as part of a broader urban nutrition strategy.

He has also worked at the SEEP Network, a non-governmental organization focused on addressing poverty, as well as Atlantic Media Company.

He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in International Relations from the College of William & Mary in Virginia.

E-mail:agoyal@email.wm.edu

Visiting Research Fellow, September 2016

Francesca Celi is a master’s degree student currently specializing in International Relations, with a focus on Central and Eastern Asia. She is a student in International Sciences in University of Turin, Italy. Her studies include politics, sociology and economics of Asia.

Audio Book – Islamic Foundations of A Free Society

发布源: Afghanistan Economic and Legal Studies Organization (AELSO) --Afghanistan | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

AELSOApril 28, 2021Audio Books

About Islamic Foundations of A Free Society:Islam is growing rapidly both in its traditional homelands and in the West. Some in the West, view Islam with a mixture of fear and suspicion. However, it is also fair to say that there is widespread ignorance about Islam, and especially about its relationship to political systems and the economy. Is Islam compatible with a free society and a free economy? Is the fact that many Muslim-majority states do not have free economies or polities a result of an incompatibility between Islam and political and economic freedom, or does it result from an unfortunate series of historical events? What role has past colonialism played in encouraging Muslim extremism? Exactly what does Islam have to say about freedom in economic, political and religious life? This book, written by a range of Islamic scholars, sheds a great deal of light on these crucial questions. It is an important book for those in the West who need to understand Islam better. It is also important for those in Muslim countries who can influence the development of political systems and economic policy.The book is edited byNouh El Harmouzi & Linda Whetstoneand fortunately, now it is translated to Dari by AELSO and it is available as Audio Book in here and as PDF inhere.This Audio Book (Islamic Foundations of A Free Society) is presented for the visually impaired, or for busy people while on the road.

Tian Shan Policy Center (TSPC) is an international non-profit institution at the American University of Central Asia (AUCA) which focuses on research, policy advisory, capacity development and project implementation.

Since its establishment in 2011 TSPC promoted the study of Central Asia at the local and international levels and government institutions as the basis for improving the lives of people in new democracies.

TSPC specializes in research on migration (internal and external), sustainable development and environmental protection, human rights, democratic governance of Central Asia.

Alongside the strong evidence based research and policy advisory, TSPC organizes high quality trainings, conferences and events on pertinent topics in the region.

At the Second Regional Dialogue on Circular Economy in Central Asia, Kyrgyzstan was represented by members of Parliament, government institutions, and the business community

On 13-14 October 2025, the Second Regional Dialogue of Central Asian Parliamentarians on Circular Economy took place in Almaty, Republic of Kazakhstan. The event was organized by the EU SWITCH-Asia Programme (Policy Support Component) in cooperation with the Regional Environmental Centre for Central Asia (CAREC). The dialogue brought together parliamentarians, representatives of ministries, international organizations, experts, and business representatives from five countries of the region - Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.

About The Adventures of Jonathan Gullible:Ken started writing economic commentaries for radio in 1980, but straight commentary from an academic economics was dry and uninteresting. No one paid any attention – and rightly so.Recalling the literary genius of Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s Travel and Antoine de Saint Exupery’s The Little Prince, Ken called upon friends to help spice up the radio spots with fantasy dialogues. Why shouldn’t economics be interesting? So Jonathan Gullible (JG) was born and interest among the radio audience soared! The ideas were outlandish and provocative so Sam Slom, President of Small Business Hawaii, proposed JG as a tool for economics education in the islands.The Adventures of Jonathan Gullible: A Free Market Odyssey has since been used for radio broadcasts, classroom discussions and debates, essay contests, film and theatrical productions, magazine and internet serialization, and animation around the globe.The book has won numerous awards and has been endorsed by renowned economists, publishers, and journalists: Milton Friedman, Walter Williams, Mark Skousen, Walter Block, Fred Foldvary, Steve Forbes, and John Stossel. It has been translated and published in more than 40 languages. Greetings of Peace & Solidarity!

The Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) is honored to share with you its First Issue ofTransitional Justice Monitorfeaturing civil society and our community partners’ initiatives to engage transitional justice issues and challenges in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

This initial issue ofTransitional Justice Monitoraims to reflect on the valuable lessons, stories, and learnings from the communities of the internally displaced persons (IDPs) or thebakwitshoping to highlight particularly the Marawi IDPs’ continuing call for a safe and dignified return and justice almost six years after the tragic Marawi siege.

Through this publication, we echo the just demands of the IDPs to the Philippine government, concerned agencies and policy actors to effect policy changes toward the rebuilding and rehabilitation of Marawi with the welfare and meaningful participation of the IDPs at the core of priorities.

Transitional Justice Monitorseeks to raise public awareness on pressing issues and challenges around the themes of transitional justice, peacebuilding, human security, conflict transformation and social justice as Transitional Justice and Reconciliation (TJR) is an integral aspect of the Annex on Normalization, a prime feature  of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB).

item.title: [Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) --Philippines] Land Rights, Displacement, and Transitional Justice in the Bangsamoro: Insights from household-level mapping in Marawi City and Maguindanao
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) --Philippines官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Land Rights, Displacement, and Transitional Justice in the Bangsamoro: Insights from household-level mapping in Marawi City and Maguindanao

发布源: Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) --Philippines | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

Land dispossession is acknowledged as a root cause of historical and contemporary conflict in the Bangsamoro that must be jointly addressed by a wide range of stakeholders: the Government of the Philippines (GPH); the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF); the recently-created Parliament of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM); relevant provincial, municipal, and barangay authorities; alongside traditional leaders, grassroots institutions, and clans. In response, this report summarizes findings from rapid community and household-level participatory and IDP-led mapping processes and dialogues conducted from late 2021 to mid-2022 in displaced neighborhoods in Marawi City, Lanao del Sur and South Upi and Firis Complex in Maguindanao. We present parcel-level evidence on the effects of protracted displacement and land tenure instability on Mranaw, Tëduray-Lambangian, and Maguindanaon internally-displaced persons (IDPs), along with concrete recommendations to aid in the resolution of land conflicts and dispossession, from the point-of-view of displaced residents themselves.

item.title: [Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) --Philippines] Transitional Justice and Reconciliation in and beyond the Bangsamoro
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) --Philippines官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Transitional Justice and Reconciliation in and beyond the Bangsamoro

发布源: Initiatives for International Dialogue (IID) --Philippines | 抓取时间: 2026-11-10

“Transitional Justice In and Beyond Bangsamoro: Research Study on Community Narratives of Resilience and Truth-telling”, is a bundled research publication and resource guide on basic concepts and narratives on how transitioning societies deal with past atrocities. We aim to see how these interlocking concepts of transitional justice (TJ), dealing with the past, justice, reconciliation, and restorative justice feed into each other in the universe of theory, practice and policy. The realm of practice is breathed into life by the stories of survival, truth seeking, and restoring relationships delicately woven in the entire documentation process.

A result of a two-year peacebuilding project of listening, dialogue, imagining and taking action towards contributing to the discourse on TJR in and beyond the Bangsamoro, this was formally presented with key actors and stakeholders during the webinar last May 31, 2021, entitled “Role of Community, Culture, and Memory : Public Presentation of Narratives and Civil Society Proposals”. This knowledge product is a salvo of civil society’s efforts in further socializing and engaging the TJR discourse, agenda, and process during the political transition.
